title: TransXplainRRG: A Radiologist-Evaluated LVLM for Chest Radiograph Report Generation.
abstract: Recent advancements in Large Vision- Language Models (LVLM) enhance X-ray report generation, but often neglect clinical context, overlook workflow integration, and lack explainability, which hinders clinical adoption due to interpretability and reliability concerns. This paper addresses the dual challenges of performance and expert explainability in automated X-ray report generation for clinical AI applications. Our proposed approach, TransXplainRRG, utilises an off-the-shelf Swin Transformer model along with a transformer-based text encoder that incorporates patient medical history to generate a radiology report. Further, we explore an expert-guided 'inside-out' approach and extract only abnormal findings for radiology report refinement. Thus, this study bridges the gap between high-performance automation and interpretability critical for clinical practice by combining state-of-the-art transformer-based vision encoders, text encoders, and LLMs. TransXplainRRG is trained and tested on the large-scale MIMIC-CXR dataset and further evaluated on the unseen IU X-Ray dataset to demonstrate its generalizability and robustness. We employed the GREEN metric as a complementary measure of clinical consistency, achieving scores of 0.327 on MIMIC-CXR and 0.605 on IU X-Ray, both higher than those achieved by MAIRA-2 under the same evaluation setting. It also performed competitively across standard evaluation metrics, frequently matching or surpassing state-of-the-art models. Additionally, we introduce qualitative evaluation metrics developed from radiologists' viewpoints and conduct a preliminary radiologist evaluation on 100 generated reports to assess their clinical relevance. Quantitative and qualitative analyses further demonstrate the potential of our TransXplainRRG framework for reliable and explainable radiology report generation.

title: DualSeg: Unified Multi-Scale Framework With Dual-Stage Encoder For Glomerular Segmentation.
abstract: Glomerular segmentation in whole-slide histopathology is essential for quantitative renal assessment, yet it is fundamentally challenged by local texture discriminability, spatial heterogeneity, and the need for multi-scale mapping of morphological priors. While convolutional neural networks address local textures via inductive biases, and Vision Transformers model global contexts through self-attention, neither paradigm simultaneously resolves these three challenges without incurring prohibitive computational overhead. Furthermore, clinical translation is frequently bottlenecked by human data scarcity. Here, we propose DualSeg, a dual-stage hybrid framework that unifies convolutional and attention capabilities through a synergistic local-to-global refinement strategy. The encoder employs Wave-Swin Blocks with dynamic propagation windows for hierarchical local feature extraction, followed by Vision Recurrent Weighted Key Value Blocks utilizing a novel Z-Shift operator for efficient, linear-complexity global context modeling. A lightweight decoder based on Non-negative Matrix Factorization subsequently fuses multi-scale features while suppressing background noise. On the murine KPIs and human HuBMAP datasets, DualSeg achieved mean DSCs of 92.98% and 89.79%, respectively. To evaluate crossspecies and cross-center generalizability under human data scarcity, we performed zero-shot inference on the KPMP dataset using models trained exclusively on murine data. DualSeg demonstrated superior generalization, validating its ability to leverage conserved mammalian morphological priors across staining domains. Code is available at https://github.com/unskye/DualSeg.

title: Physics-Informed Implicit Neural Representations in Biomedical Tomography: Principles, Applications, and Reliability.
abstract: Biomedical tomography reconstructs spatially and temporally varying images or biophysical fields from indirect measurements governed by acquisition physics. Physics-informed implicit neural representations (INRs) parameterize these unknowns as coordinate-conditioned neural fields, optionally incorporating physical states, and estimate their parameters through measurement consistency. Despite growing adoption, the specific contributions of INRs are often conflated with those of forward modeling, continuous representation, and neural priors, obscuring when they offer substantive advantages. This review adopts a representation-physics-inference perspective to clarify the role of INRs relative to conventional voxel, basis, and other neural parameterizations. We examine how coordinate and state conditioning provide a direct interface to the forward model, while shared network parameters couple reconstruction updates across queried locations and states. Starting from scan-specific INR reconstruction, we identify three limitations: insufficient measurement information, modeling uncertainty, and the computational burden. Corresponding advances are organized into prior-enhanced reconstruction, joint estimation of target fields and physical variables, and scalable or amortized inference. Using representative examples from CT, MRI, ultrasound, photoacoustic imaging, PET, and optical tomography, we assess how these strategies affect reconstruction bias, identifiability, quantitative reliability, and computational efficiency. We distinguish essential, enabling, or merely incidental INR roles according to their coupling with acquisition physics. This perspective clarifies the opportunities and limitations of physics-informed INRs and identifies forward-model fidelity, solution identifiability, scalable inference, and independent quantitative and clinical validation as development priorities.

title: Beyond Morphology: Quantitative Bilateral Self-Referenced Frequency-Domain Diffuse Optical Spectroscopy Reveals Functional Abnormalities in Patellar Tendinopathy.
abstract: Objective Patellar tendinopathy (PT) involves functional and metabolic abnormalities that may precede structural degeneration, whereas MRI and ultrasonography primarily depict morphology. To bridge this gap, we aim to develop a quantitative optical method for detecting PT-related functional and hemodynamic abnormalities. Methods We developed an embedded multi-wavelength frequency-domain diffuse optical spectroscopy system integrating sinusoidal modulation, synchronized acquisition, real-time Goertzel demodulation, optical-property inversion, chromophore fitting, and standardized grid scanning over the patellar tendon region. To reduce inter-subject variability, a bilateral self-referenced strategy used the contralateral tendon as an endogenous reference. A composite optical biomarker, Tendon Hemodynamic Index (THI), was defined by integrating differential tissue oxygenation and blood-volume-related information. Results Phantom and in vivo measurements demonstrated robust quantitative performance. In a clinical cohort, THI was significantly elevated in PT patients and correlated with symptom severity and functional impairment across the full cohort, with Spearman correlations of 0.69 with the Numeric Rating Scale and -0.74 with the Victorian Institute of Sport Assessment-Patella score. In this exploratory cohort, THI distinguished PT from healthy controls with 91.8% accuracy, 95.8% sensitivity, 88.0% specificity, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.928. In imaging negative but symptom-positive cases, THI achieved 88.2% classification accuracy. In three exploratory follow-up cases, THI decreased toward the bilateral baseline as symptoms improved over 8 weeks. Conclusion The proposed method enables self-referenced quantification of PT-related functional abnormalities. Significance By revealing tendon hemodynamic abnormalities beyond structural imaging, this work supports early PT detection, objective severity assessment, and quantitative monitoring of disease recovery.

Methods

We developed an embedded multi-wavelength frequency-domain diffuse optical spectroscopy system integrating sinusoidal modulation, synchronized acquisition, real-time Goertzel demodulation, optical-property inversion, chromophore fitting, and standardized grid scanning over the patellar tendon region. To reduce inter-subject variability, a bilateral self-referenced strategy used the contralateral tendon as an endogenous reference. Phantom and in vivo measurements demonstrated robust quantitative performance. In a clinical cohort, THI was significantly elevated in PT patients and correlated with symptom severity and functional impairment across the full cohort, with Spearman correlations of 0.69 with the Numeric Rating Scale and -0.74 with the Victorian Institute of Sport Assessment-Patella score. In imaging negative but symptom-positive cases, THI achieved 88.2% classification accuracy. In three exploratory follow-up cases, THI decreased toward the bilateral baseline as symptoms improved over 8 weeks.

Conclusion

The proposed method enables self-referenced quantification of PT-related functional abnormalities.

Significance

By revealing tendon hemodynamic abnormalities beyond structural imaging, this work supports early PT detection, objective severity assessment, and quantitative monitoring of disease recovery.

title: Surrogate Supervision for Robust and Generalizable Deformable Image Registration.
abstract: Objective Deep learning-based deformable image registration has achieved strong accuracy, but remains sensitive to variations in input image characteristics such as artifacts, anatomical content mismatch, or modality difference. We aim to develop a general training paradigm that improves the robustness and generalizability of registration networks. Methods We introduce surrogate supervision, which decouples the input domain from the supervision domain by applying estimated spatial transformations to surrogate images. This allows training on heterogeneous inputs while ensuring supervision is computed in domains where similarity is well defined. We evaluate the framework through three representative applications: artifact-robust brain MR registration, mask-agnostic lung CT registration, and multi-modal MR registration. Results Across tasks, surrogate supervision demonstrated strong resilience to input variations, including inhomogeneity field, inconsistent anatomical content, and modality differences, while generally maintaining competitive performance on well-curated in-domain data. Conclusions Surrogate supervision provides a principled framework for training robust and generalizable deep learning-based registration models without increasing complexity. Significance Surrogate supervision offers a practical pathway to more robust and generalizable medical image registration, enabling broader applicability in diverse biomedical imaging scenarios.

title: Synergizing SAM2 and U-Mamba as Mutual Teachers in a Dual-Branch Dynamic Knowledge Transfer Network for Orbital Segmentation.
abstract: Accurate segmentation of orbital structures in thyroid eye disease (TED) is critical for clinical staging and surgical planning. However, as an under-explored task, orbital multi-organ segmentation suffers from inherent data scarcity, resulting in substantial domain gaps when directly applying general-purpose segmentation models. These foundation models often lack sufficient exposure to orbital imaging data, producing anatomically implausible yet overconfident predictions. To address this challenge, we propose a Dual-Branch Dynamic Knowledge Transfer Network (DDKTN), which integrates the global semantic generalization capability of SAM2 with the fine-grained structural modeling strength of U-Mamba. Specifically, a Dynamic Feature Interaction (DFI) mechanism enables adaptively controlled inter-branch knowledge transfer, facilitating a progressive transition from SAM2-guided global semantics to U-Mamba-driven structural refinement. Moreover, a Bidirectional Consensus Confidence (BCC) regularization mechanism identifies consensus and discrepancy regions between the foundation and domain-specific branches, enforcing anatomy-aware consistency via mutual supervision. In addition, a Prompt Adaptation Module (PAM) leverages the anatomical sensitivity of the domain-specific branch to automatically generate structured prompts, thereby injecting reliable anatomical priors into SAM2. Experiments conducted on a private orbital CT dataset and a public coronal MRI benchmark demonstrate that DDKTN achieves superior performance, with average Dice scores of 93.68% and 94.65%, respectively. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of each component in improving generalization and anatomical fidelity. The implementation of our method is available at https://github.com/zltshadow/DDKTN.

title: SSFMamba: Learning Symmetry-driven Spatial-Frequency Modeling for Physically Consistent 3D Medical Image Segmentation.
abstract: Accurate 3D medical image segmentation requires a delicate balance between fine-grained local details and global contextual understanding. While spatial-domain models often struggle with long-range dependencies, existing frequency-based approaches frequently overlook intrinsic spectral properties such as Hermitian symmetry, leading to suboptimal feature integration. In this paper, we propose SSFMamba, a Mamba based Symmetry-driven Spatial-Frequency fusion framework tailored for 3D medical imaging. Our architecture employs a complementary dual-branch design: the spatial branch preserves intricate anatomical textures, while the frequency branch captures global contextual dependencies in the frequency domain. A core innovation is the 3D Multi-Directional Scanning Mechanism (MDSM), which integrates Hermitian symmetry with the causal nature of State Space Models (SSMs) to enable direction-aware global modeling. Crucially, by shifting the modeling focus to frequency-domain spectral components, SSFMamba captures the underlying structural characteristics of anatomical tissues. This leads to a highly adaptable framework that excels in both MRI and CT applications, regardless of the significant variations in intensity distributions. Extensive evaluations on the BraTS2020, BraTS2023, and BTCV datasets demonstrate that SSFMamba consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Notably, our approach achieves exceptional performance on low-contrast organs such as the pancreas (81.97% Dice), underscoring its potential as a unified and physically consistent perception framework for diverse 3D clinical applications.

title: Identification of local nonlinear shear-wave dynamics using Volterra kernels: application to prostate cancer detection.
abstract: Cancer remains a major health concern worldwide. Shear-wave elastography (SWE) holds promise for cancer detection by quantifying linear elastic changes in tissue through shear-wave (SW) velocity estimation. However, shear viscosity and nonlinearity are often over-looked, despite their potential as additional biomarkers. This study evaluates the visco-hyperelastic properties of soft tissue, including linear shear modulus, shear viscosity, and shear nonlinearity. We propose using Volterra kernels to characterize local nonlinear SW dynamics, with kernel identification based on SW particle velocity measurements at adjacent locations. The method was validated using in-silico simulations and in-vitro gelatin phantoms. To evaluate its clinical relevance, we applied the method for prostate cancer (PCa) detection. To our knowledge, this is the first in-vivo assessment of voxel-based visco-hyperelastic properties of the prostate. In 90 patients, our results indicated that the linear kernel correlated with the linear shear modulus, while the quadratic kernel reflected both viscosity and nonlinearity. A convolutional neural network trained on these parameters with registered histopathology as ground truth achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.60 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.57, 0.62) and 0.66 (95% CI: 0.64, 0.68) for PCa detection, respectively-both significantly outperforming the linear shear modulus (AUC of 0.54; 95% CI, 0.52 to 0.56). Our findings suggest that Volterra kernels reflect information related to the visco-hyperelastic properties of prostate tissue, highlighting the potential of viscosity and nonlinearity as additional biomarkers for PCa detection.
authorString: Li X, Turco S, Zwart M, Beerlage HP, Wijkstra H, Mischi M.

title: Boundary-Ambiguity-Aware Lesion Evidence Learning for Breast Ultrasound Segmentation and Multimodal Classification.
abstract: Multimodal analysis of breast ultrasound images and structured clinical data can support lesion characterization across diverse clinical classification tasks. However, existing image and clinicopathological data fusion methods usually fuse imaging and clinical information as feature vectors, without explicitly organizing ultrasound-derived evidence according to anatomical roles such as the lesion core, ambiguous boundary and peritumoral tissue. Therefore, this paper proposes a boundary-ambiguity-aware lesion evidence learning framework (BAA-LEL) for joint breast ultrasound lesion segmentation and multimodal classification. BAA-LEL first extracts a lesion prior with a MedSAM-assisted segmentation branch and refines ambiguous margins through an anchor-constrained boundary graph. The refined lesion prior is organized into core, boundary, and peritumoral regions, while boundary geometry and ambiguity are retained as complementary evidence. A morphology-clinical heterogeneous graph then models interactions among regional morphology, boundary evidence, and structured clinical variables for task-specific classification. Experiments on HER2USC, LNMUSC, BrEaST, BUSI, and ISIC IMA++ demonstrate strong segmentation performance and competitive classification performance across breast ultrasound and cross-domain settings. Controlled ablations, statistical comparisons, calibration analysis, and interpretability experiments further support the contributions of boundary-aware refinement, zonal morphology encoding, and morphology-clinical heterogeneous reasoning. The source code is available at: https://github.com/JinlinYY/BAA-LEL.

title: CPCLNet: Advancing Cross-Modal Few-Shot Medical Image Segmentation with Clustering-Inspired Prototype Consistency Learning.
abstract: Cross-modal few-shot medical image segmentation (FSMIS) provides a solution for alleviating annotation scarcity and improving generalization across imaging modalities. However, severe modality discrepancy can disrupt support-query matching, contaminate support-derived foreground and background prototypes, and produce noisy affinity maps, making target-modality segmentation unreliable. To address this problem, we propose CPCLNet, a clustering-inspired prototype consistency learning network for cross-modal FSMIS. CPCLNet formulates cross-modal segmentation as a prototype consistency learning problem and progressively improves feature-space consistency, prototype reliability, and affinity-map coherence. Specifically, a parameter-sharing feature encoder provides a common representation basis across modalities, and a cross-modal distribution alignment module performs episode-specific support-query alignment. A clustering-inspired representative prototype descriptor further suppresses unstable support responses and constructs compact, modality-robust prototypes. Finally, an RWKV-based affinity map prediction module propagates prototype-guided correspondence across long-range spatial contexts with linear complexity. Extensive experiments on three imaging modalities, demonstrate that CPCLNet outperforms existing methods, achieving an average Dice improvement of 3.34 percentage points over the second-best competitor across CT→MRI and CT→PET tasks under both 1-shot and 5-shot settings. Further integration with MedSAM yields consistent improvements, indicating CP-CLNet's complementary potential with foundation models.

title: Clinical-SAM: Agentic Test-Time Adaptation of SAM via Physician-in-the-Loop for Clinical Tumor Segmentation.
abstract: Interactive foundation models such as SAM struggle to generalize across clinical deployment sites. Among existing adaptation strategies, test-time adaptation (TTA) is the most promising, yet current TTA methods trade one problem for another: removing the physician eliminates clinical grounding, while retaining the physician reintroduces a costly annotation burden. In this work, we propose Clinical-SAM, a two-phase agentic physician-in-the-loop TTA framework that teaches a frozen SAM to approximate what a physician would accept - directly and continuously, without requiring spatial annotations. In Phase I (pre-deployment), a self-prompting agent trained via reinforcement learning generates prompts autonomously, eliminating per-case expert spatial input at inference. In Phase II (deployment), the agent policy is refined online by the one signal physicians already produce: a binary accept/reject feedback on each proposed mask. As the binary feedback accumulates across deployed cases, the agent converges toward a policy that produces masks meeting a reference acceptance standard designed to approximate physician judgment, with progressively fewer interactions. We evaluate Clinical-SAM in a pre-clinical setting on six oncological benchmarks spanning CT (colon, pancreas, liver, kidney) and PET (head & neck, lung) tumor segmentation, using agreement with reference-standard segmentations as a proxy for physician acceptance. Clinical-SAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on all six datasets, outperforming fine-tuning, interactive, TTA, and online-learning baselines, while requiring only 3.3 binary judgments per case on average across the six datasets. Our code is available here.

title: One-Step Rectified Flow Reconstruction with Spectral Weighting for Limited-angle Cardiac CT.
abstract: Limited-angle cardiac computed tomography (CT) suffers from severe directional artifacts and resolution degradation due to missing wedges in the frequency domain. Diffusion-based reconstruction methods have demonstrated strong artifact suppression capabilities but typically require iterative sampling at a high computational cost. To accelerate limited-angle CT reconstruction, we propose a rectified-flow framework trained with paired supervision for fast inference. Instead of generating images from Gaussian noise, the model learns a deterministic transport from artifact-contaminated Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) reconstructions to full-view reference images. A 2.5D slice-context modeling strategy is introduced to exploit inter-slice information while reconstructing only the central slice, improving structural consistency. Furthermore, we introduce a reconstruction-aware spectral loss that applies frequency-domain supervision to an approximate endpoint reconstruction inferred from the predicted flow velocity. By embedding spectral priors into the learning objective and using one-step rectified-flow inference (a single network evaluation), the proposed framework achieves fast reconstruction while preserving image fidelity. Experiments on XCAT simulations and clinical cardiac CT data show superior quantitative performance and substantially reduced inference time compared to the state-of-the-art baselines. A qualitative review by an experienced cardiac radiologist further suggests improved visualization of motion-sensitive coronary structures with reduced motion blur.
authorString: Han S, Fang C, Morovati B, Zhou L, Li H, Ni S, Fan S, Terry JG, Carr JJ, Wang G, Yu H.

title: A Robust Physics-Informed Implicit Neural Representation for Speed-of-Sound Image Reconstruction in USCT.
abstract: As a promising imaging modality, ultrasound computed tomography (USCT) holds significant clinical value by providing quantitative parametric maps, such as speed of sound (SOS), in addition to high-resolution anatomical structures. While full-waveform inversion (FWI) is optimal for high-fidelity SOS reconstruction, its severe non-convexity frequently causes traditional discrete grid-based methods to trap in local minima, yielding anatomical artifacts that hinder clinical translation. Here, we propose POLARIS, an unsupervised continuous neural field inversion framework that utilizes spatial continuity as implicit regularization to stabilize the complex FWI optimization. Tailored to the circular acquisition geometry of USCT, we design a scale-aware radially-modulated polar encoding that effectively mitigates radial-angular sampling non-uniformity. We leverage the deterministic nature of the coupling background velocity to extract anatomical boundaries directly from acoustic signals, serving as a structural prior to preserve tissue integrity. Optimization is facilitated by a stochastic shot-batched optimization strategy, leveraging global parameter coupling to update the SOS field from subset emissions and accelerate convergence. Extensive validations on numerical and in vivo breast and musculoskeletal data demonstrate the POLARIS's higher accuracy and structural fidelity. Comparisons with MRI confirm the high anatomical consistency of the reconstructed SOS images. Notably, the framework maintains robust reconstruction performance under sparse-view configurations, highlighting its potential for accelerated USCT acquisition with reduced measurement requirements.

title: Does More Speech Therapy Lead to Better Results in Childhood Apraxia of Speech? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of the Available Evidence.
abstract: Background In recent years there has been a significant increase in the number and quality of childhood apraxia of speech (CAS) treatment research published. Much of this research has focussed on establishing treatment efficacy and identifying treatment components. A smaller subset of the literature has looked at treatment intensity, such as comparing therapy delivered twice per week with four times per week, however this literature has not been compared across interventions. Aims This systematic review and meta-analysis examines cumulative intervention intensity and its components (dose per session, dose frequency, intervention duration-number of weeks) and reported treatment effects to understand whether there is a relationship between dose and effect in specific treatments or overall. Methods A systematic search and review was registered with Prospero (CRD420251107259). Twelve electronic databases were searched supplemented by handsearching references lists. Included studies were coded for CAS diagnosis confidence, methodological quality, dose characteristics, and treatment outcomes. Standard mean difference (SMD), an effect size metric equivalent to Cohen's d, was calculated for 25 included papers and weighted Pearson's correlations performed to identify relationships between dose characteristics and treatment outcomes. Main contribution This paper is the first to (1) create omnibus standard effect sizes across diverse interventions and (2) show the relationship between intensity and treatment outcome in children with CAS. The omnibus SMD across studies with three or more participants for treated items was 1.22 (confidence interval 0.76-1.67), a large effect, and for generalisation items was 0.66 (confidence interval 0.46-0.85) which is a moderate effect. These results show that CAS treatment works in well-controlled studies when delivered at least twice per week for at least 45 min per session. The relationship between intensity variables and generalisation SMD was less clear with weeks of therapy being moderately correlated (r = 0.39) and none of the other variables showing any relationship with study SMD. These results should be interpreted carefully as there was significant missing data and limited range in some variables. Researchers need to include more standard intensity information in reporting their results. Conclusions Treatment for CAS is effective and leads to moderate generalisation; more weeks of therapy leads to stronger gains than fewer weeks of therapy. What this paper adds What is already known on this subject CAS is a neurological-based motor speech disorder that originates in childhood for which there are a number of effective treatments. For this population, high intensity treatment is recommended-over 100 production trials per session, 2-5 sessions per week, across an extended period. In studies which directly compare intensity of variables, more therapy (e.g. 20 sessions) results in greater improvement than less therapy (e.g. 10 sessions). There are no previous meta-analyses of intensity variables-dose, dose frequency, treatment duration, or cumulative intervention intensity in CAS What this study adds to the existing knowledge This study compiles data from 25 studies with a low risk of bias and high CAS diagnostic confidence in a meta-analysis of the dose effects of CAS treatment. The meta-analysis shows that CAS treatment in general works. Most studies had 2-4 sessions per week across 3-12 weeks. Within this narrow band of intensity, a significant correlation was shown between the number of weeks of therapy and outcome. There is no significant evidence for CAS therapy less frequently than twice per week at this time. Eight different treatments demonstrated efficacy for improving speech outcomes in children with CAS. What are the clinical implications of this study? Provided they are delivered at least twice per week for at least 12 sessions, with greater improvements when treatment extends over more weeks, selection of any of the included treatments should result in improved speech where the child being treated is similar to children in the research. The following treatments were shown to be effective for CAS: Integral stimulation treatments including Dynamic Temporal and Tactile Cueing, Kaufman-Speech to Language Protocol, Motor Speech Treatment Protocol, Nuffield Dyspraxia Programme-3rd Edition, Rapid Syllable Transition Treatment, Speech Motor Chaining and Ultrasound Biofeedback alone and the combination of Speech Motor Chaining with Ultrasound Biofeedback. Practitioner points Therapy must be sufficiently frequent and sustained: Evidence shows that CAS treatment is effective when therapy is provided at least twice per week, over a minimum of 12 sessions, for 45 min per session with total weeks of therapy being the only intensity variable consistently associated with treatment outcomes. Dose matters, both within and across sessions: Clinicians should prioritise the number of production trials and ensure adequate cumulative intervention intensity. Sessions with low active practice time or insufficient trials are unlikely to produce meaningful change. Eight treatments are effective for CAS: Integral Stimulation including Dynamic Temporal and Tactile Cueing (DTTC), Kaufman Speech to Language Program (K-SLP), Motor Speech Treatment Protocol (MSTP), Nuffield Dyspraxia Programme (3rd ed; NDP3), Rapid Syllable Transition Treatment (ReST), Speech Motor Chaining (SMC), Ultrasound Biofeedback, and SMC + Ultrasound Biofeedback combined. Clinicians should consider the client's speech needs and overall profile when selecting from the treatments that have demonstrated effectiveness.

Sessions with low active practice time or insufficient trials are unlikely to produce meaningful change. Eight treatments are effective for CAS: Integral Stimulation including Dynamic Temporal and Tactile Cueing (DTTC), Kaufman Speech to Language Program (K-SLP), Motor Speech Treatment Protocol (MSTP), Nuffield Dyspraxia Programme (3rd ed; NDP3), Rapid Syllable Transition Treatment (ReST), Speech Motor Chaining (SMC), Ultrasound Biofeedback, and SMC + Ultrasound Biofeedback combined. Clinicians should consider the client's speech needs and overall profile when selecting from the treatments that have demonstrated effectiveness.

title: Prognostic Value of Early Dynamic Changes in Skeletal Muscle Index for Unresectable Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Prospective Landmark Analysis.
abstract: Objectives To investigate the prognostic value of early dynamic skeletal muscle index (ΔSMI) changes in unresectable lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) and explore associations with systemic inflammatory and nutritional markers. Materials and methods This prospective study enrolled 76 patients with unresectable Stage III/IV LUSC. Routine computed tomography images at the fourth thoracic vertebra were analyzed before and 90 days posttreatment to quantify body composition changes. Progression-free survival (PFS) was evaluated using landmark analysis to prevent immortal time bias. Multivariate Cox regression identified independent prognostic factors utilizing optimal cut-offs from the maxstat algorithm. Results Only rapid skeletal muscle depletion (ΔSMI ≤ -5.0%) emerged as an independent predictor of adverse PFS (HR = 2.030, 95% CI: 1.132-3.642, p = 0.018), alongside clinical Stage IV (p < 0.001); overall ΔBMI lacked prognostic significance. Patients with rapid muscle loss exhibited persistently elevated C-reactive protein and steeper hemoglobin declines, reflecting an unresolved inflammatory and hypercatabolic state. Subgroup analyses confirmed ΔSMI's consistent prognostic value across age, sex, and stage (all P-interaction > 0.05). Conclusion Early ΔSMI loss, not overall weight variation, independently predicts poor PFS in unresectable LUSC. Routine CT-based body composition monitoring provides a critical window to identify high-risk patients for interventions targeting the muscle-inflammation axis. Trial registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2500104777.

title: WIse CHoices in the ICU (WICH-ICU): Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan for a Stepped-Wedge Cluster Randomized Trial of Choosing Wisely Interventions in Swedish Intensive Care Units.
abstract: Background Healthcare overuse, including unnecessary diagnostic testing and procedures, contributes to patient harm, increased healthcare costs, and resource waste. The Choosing Wisely initiative aims to reduce low-value care through evidence-based recommendations. However, limited evidence exists regarding the safety and effectiveness of implementing Choosing Wisely recommendations in intensive care settings. Methods The WICH-ICU is a registry-based stepped-wedge cluster randomized controlled trial designed to evaluate the implementation of specific Choosing Wisely interventions in Swedish intensive care units (ICUs). The study will include adult patients treated in participating Swedish ICUs. The intervention consists of three parts of the Choosing Wisely recommendations: (1) reduced frequency of arterial blood gas sampling, (2) reduced routine laboratory testing, and (3) reduced routine chest radiography. The primary outcome is 30-day mortality. Secondary outcomes include ICU length of stay, duration of mechanical ventilation (invasive and noninvasive), continuous renal replacement therapy duration, and ICU readmission within 72 h. Intervention data, testing intensity (arterial blood gas samples, laboratory tests, and chest radiographs per patient-day), will be collected through local monitoring, while outcome data will be obtained from the Swedish Intensive Care Registry (SIR). The stepped-wedge design allows each participating ICU to serve as its own control, with randomized timing of intervention implementation. Discussion This study will provide evidence on the safety and effectiveness of implementing Choosing Wisely recommendations in intensive care settings. The stepped-wedge cluster randomized design minimizes contamination while allowing all participating sites to eventually receive the intervention. The results will inform evidence-based de-implementation strategies in critical care. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT07013175.

title: Long-Term Fate of Resorbed Adjacent Teeth Associated With Impacted Maxillary Canines Following Orthodontic Treatment: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Limited evidence exists on the long-term prognosis of resorptive lesions in teeth adjacent to impacted maxillary canines' post-orthodontic treatment. To systematically evaluate the long-term radiographic status of resorbed maxillary incisor roots following orthodontic correction of adjacent ectopically erupting canines. Comprehensive electronic and manual searches across five databases identified retrospective or prospective studies assessing long-term Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) or radiographic follow-up of resorbed adjacent teeth. Data selection, extraction and bias assessment were performed independently. Five studies with moderate risk of bias met inclusion criteria. The combined sample consisted of 54 male and 123 female. Findings indicate that orthodontic management of impacted canines carries minimal risk of progressive root resorption or periodontal deterioration in adjacent incisors. Resorbed incisors largely retained vitality and functional stability, with no mobility beyond Grade 1 and resorption lacunae often became shallower over time. Marked heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Long-term outcomes are favourable, with most resorbed root surfaces showing natural remodelling and minimal need for endodontic intervention. title: Clinical Trial: Capsule Sponge as a Non-Endoscopic Monitoring Tool in Eosinophilic Oesophagitis-A Prospective Real-World Multicentre Study.
abstract: Background and aims Eosinophilic oesophagitis (EoE) is a chronic inflammatory condition requiring repeat endoscopy and biopsy for histological monitoring, which is invasive, resource-intensive and burdensome for patients. The capsule sponge (CS) offers a potential non-invasive alternative. We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy, feasibility and patient acceptability of CS versus endoscopic biopsies for monitoring disease activity in adult patients. Methods A real-world prospective multicentre cohort study was conducted across three NHS sites in England from August 2023 to June 2025. Adults with established EoE without oesophageal strictures underwent same-day endoscopy and CS using the Endosign device. Histological activity was defined as ≥ 15 eosinophils per high-power field or 0.3 mm 2 on endoscopic biopsy histology and CS respectively. Symptom burden was assessed using the Dysphagia Symptom Questionnaire, endoscopic severity using the EoE Endoscopic Reference Score and patient acceptability via structured questionnaire. Results 136 patients (164 paired episodes) from three secondary care hospitals successfully swallowed CS with sufficient sampling; CS swallowing success rate was 92.7%. Median age was 45 years (IQR 34.8-56); 92/136 (67.6%) were male. CS demonstrated sensitivity 76.3%, specificity 89.5%, PPV 80.4%, NPV 87.0% and overall accuracy 84.8% (Cohen's κ = 0.67). AUC was 0.904 (95% CI 0.856-0.953). Patient acceptability recorded 96.7% found CS acceptable, 78.8% preferred it over endoscopy, and 90.8% would repeat the procedure. No complications occurred. Conclusions CS is a safe, feasible, accurate and highly acceptable less-invasive tool for monitoring EoE. Its implementation could improve care pathways, reducing the need for repeated endoscopic biopsies while maintaining diagnostic reliability, with potential to reduce service burden, carbon emissions and improve patient experience. Trial registration CoSiE: IRAS number: 314770; ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06501274; QuBiE: UK Clinical Trial registry identifier: ISRCTN14071734; Trial number: 10083253.

title: Association of Polygenic Risk Score for Suicidal Behavior With Ventral Prefrontal Morphology in Bipolar Disorder.
abstract: Background Bipolar disorder (BD) studies consistently implicate the ventral prefrontal cortex (VPFC) in association with suicidal behaviors. A suicidal behavior polygenic risk score (PRS) can now be computed to test whether elevated genetic risk for suicidal behavior is associated with variation in VPFC gray matter and/or suicidal behavior history. Methods We explored relationships among a PRS previously associated with suicidal behavior, VPFC morphology, and suicidal behavior in 376 individuals of European ancestry (mean age 30y; 57% female): 225 with BD (76 suicide attempters (SAs), 149 non-suicide attempters (NSAs)) and 151 healthy control individuals (HCs). We calculated PRS and performed magnetic resonance imaging to assess VPFC (inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) and orbitofrontal cortex) cortical thickness and surface area. Associations were examined among PRS, diagnosis, suicide attempt history, and brain measures. Results Among individuals with BD, those with higher PRS showed decreased right VPFC surface area, primarily due to IFG reductions (p < 0.01). A significant group (SA, NSA, HC)-by-PRS interaction was observed for right IFG cortical surface area (p < 0.05); NSAs with high vs. low PRS had significantly smaller right IFG surface area. The mean PRS was highest for SAs, then NSAs, and lowest for HCs; however, differences did not reach significance. Conclusions These findings suggest this suicide PRS may reflect genetic mechanisms influencing IFG differences in BD. Given the modest sample size, replication of these preliminary findings in large-scale diverse cohorts is required to determine whether including this PRS and/or the corresponding IFG values could improve multimodal BD suicidal behavior prediction algorithms.

title: Automated urine analysis of atypical urothelial cells for urothelial carcinoma: a prospective study.
abstract: Objectives To prospectively evaluate the diagnostic value of atypical urothelial cells (Atyp.C), an automatically determined quantitative parameter of the Sysmex UF-5000 urine particle analyser (Sysmex Corp., Kobe, Japan), as a non-invasive biomarker for urothelial carcinoma (UC). Early diagnosis of UC remains challenging despite advances in diagnostic techniques. While non-invasive urine cytology has high diagnostic value, clinical evidence for Atyp.C in urine remains unclear. Quantification of Atyp.C in urine may improve non-invasive UC disease diagnostics. Patients and methods Urine samples from 234 patients who underwent invasive urological intervention for non-malignant conditions (control group [CG]) or UC (intervention group [IG]) were considered. Based on histopathology, the IG was subclassified into low-grade (LG) and high-grade (HG) UC and was further grouped into non-muscle-invasive (non-MI) and MI UC. Patients who received neoadjuvant chemotherapy were analysed separately. Atyp.C of ≥0.1 Atyp.C/μL were defined as positive and were automatically quantified using the Sysmex UF-5000 urine particle analyser, which classifies epithelial cells with disproportionately high nucleic acid content relative to cell size. Smoking state, urinary tract infection (UTI), and micro-/macrohaematuria, were evaluated as potential confounding factors. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess explorative diagnostic Atyp.C performance. Results The Atyp.C concentration was higher in the IG than in the CG (mean [SEM] 0.53 [0.1] vs 0.29 [0.1] Atyp.C/μL; P = 0.004), with a sensitivity of 0.59. HGUC exhibited higher Atyp.C levels (mean [SEM] 0.85 [0.2] Atyp.C/μL, P < 0.001) and a sensitivity of 0.73. MI UC showed the highest Atyp.C concentrations (mean [SEM] 0.95 [0.4] Atyp.C/μL; P = 0.004) and sensitivity of 0.78. ROC analysis demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy for MI UC (area under the ROC curve = 0.75). ROC analysis was exploratory and lacked external validation. UTI was a significant confounder for Atyp.C quantification. Conclusion The Atyp.C are elevated in HGUC, particularly in MI disease, supporting their potential as a non-invasive diagnostic biomarker in UC condition.

title: Longitudinal genital growth curves in adolescents and Doppler-based varicocele risk stratification.
abstract: Objectives To construct longitudinal ultrasound-based growth curves for genital development and to assess the prognostic value of varicocele grade and Doppler features. Varicoceles affect ~20% of adolescent boys and can be associated with impaired fertility. Evidence-based criteria for intervention are lacking due to limited longitudinal data. Subjects, patients and methods We conducted a prospective longitudinal cohort study (2015-2021) of 570 boys aged 10.5-18 years (407 controls, 163 with left-sided varicocele; 1352 assessments). The boys underwent Tanner pubic hair staging (TSP), measurement of stretched penile length (SPL), and a scrotal ultrasound. The volumes of the left and right testes and total testicular volume (TTV) were calculated according to the Lambert formula. In varicocele, venous diameter (VD), spontaneous reflux (SR), peak retrograde flow (PRF), and clinical grade were measured. Growth trajectories were analysed using mixed-effects models. Results Severe subgroups (VD ≥3 mm, SR >20 cm/s, or Grade 3) had attenuated growth slopes and lower TTV at TSP 5 vs controls. Combined risk profiles (e.g., Grade 3 + VD ≥3 mm; SR >20 cm/s + Grade 3) showed the poorest outcomes, with final TTV consistently <30 mL. A PRF >38.4 cm/s alone was not predictive. The SPL differences were minimal. Some subgroups entered puberty earlier but progressed more slowly. Limitations include absence of semen and hormonal data, exclusion of atypical developmental disorders, and limited ethnic diversity. Conclusions Most adolescents with a varicocele develop normally. Only those with combined high-risk Doppler and clinical features show impaired testicular growth. Doppler adds prognostic value beyond grade and supports a stratified surveillance strategy, potentially reducing overtreatment.
originalAbstract:
Objectives

To construct longitudinal ultrasound-based growth curves for genital development and to assess the prognostic value of varicocele grade and Doppler features. Varicoceles affect ~20% of adolescent boys and can be associated with impaired fertility. Evidence-based criteria for intervention are lacking due to limited longitudinal data.

Subjects, patients and methods

We conducted a prospective longitudinal cohort study (2015-2021) of 570 boys aged 10.5-18 years (407 controls, 163 with left-sided varicocele; 1352 assessments). The boys underwent Tanner pubic hair staging (TSP), measurement of stretched penile length (SPL), and a scrotal ultrasound. The volumes of the left and right testes and total testicular volume (TTV) were calculated according to the Lambert formula. In varicocele, venous diameter (VD), spontaneous reflux (SR), peak retrograde flow (PRF), and clinical grade were measured. Growth trajectories were analysed using mixed-effects models.

Results

Severe subgroups (VD ≥3 mm, SR >20 cm/s, or Grade 3) had attenuated growth slopes and lower TTV at TSP 5 vs controls. Combined risk profiles (e.g., Grade 3 + VD ≥3 mm; SR >20 cm/s + Grade 3) showed the poorest outcomes, with final TTV consistently <30 mL. A PRF >38.4 cm/s alone was not predictive. The SPL differences were minimal. Some subgroups entered puberty earlier but progressed more slowly. Limitations include absence of semen and hormonal data, exclusion of atypical developmental disorders, and limited ethnic diversity.

Conclusions

Most adolescents with a varicocele develop normally. Only those with combined high-risk Doppler and clinical features show impaired testicular growth. Doppler adds prognostic value beyond grade and supports a stratified surveillance strategy, potentially reducing overtreatment.

title: DFDBA With or Without Platelet-Rich Fibrin in Maxillary Sinus Augmentation: A Randomized Split-Mouth Clinical Trial.
abstract: Objectives To compare histologic and histomorphometric outcomes after bilateral lateral maxillary sinus augmentation with demineralized freeze-dried bone allograft (DFDBA) alone versus DFDBA combined with platelet-rich fibrin (PRF), and to report 1-year prosthetic follow-up of the restored implants. Materials and methods This randomized split-mouth clinical trial included subjects requiring bilateral lateral maxillary sinus augmentation before implant placement. In each subject, one sinus was randomly assigned to DFDBA alone and the contralateral sinus to DFDBA combined with leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF) and injectable PRF (i-PRF). Bone biopsy specimens were harvested at the clinically relevant 6-month implant placement time point. The primary outcome was newly formed bone. Secondary histomorphometric outcomes were residual graft material, connective tissue, and fibrosis; inflammation and necrosis were assessed histologically. Clinical and radiographic prosthetic follow-up was performed 1 year after definitive prosthetic loading. Paired comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Results Of 24 enrolled subjects, 21 completed follow-up and contributed 42 sinus sites to the paired analysis. Median newly formed bone was 48.72% (IQR, 33.33%-63.33%) on the PRF side and 45.76% (IQR, 37.14%-54.90%) on the non-PRF side (p = 0.5). Residual graft material was 6.74% versus 4.23% (p = 0.2), connective tissue was 31.48% versus 36.92% (p = 0.016), and fibrosis was 3.42% versus 2.56% (p > 0.9). No inflammation or necrosis was observed. Following replacement of one implant that failed before prosthetic loading, all definitively restored implants remained functional during the 1-year prosthetic follow-up. Clinical and radiographic follow-up was uneventful, and no biologic or prosthetic complications requiring intervention were observed. Conclusions Adding PRF to DFDBA did not significantly increase newly formed bone at the 6-month implant placement time point. The lower connective tissue proportion on the PRF side may suggest altered tissue maturation; however, this secondary finding should be interpreted cautiously. Definitively restored implants showed 100% prosthetic survival during 1-year follow-up. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07348198; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07348198. This clinical trial was not registered prior to participant recruitment and randomization.

title: Fully automated AI-based quantification of tumour volume on PSMA PET-CT images is associated with overall survival in prostate cancer.
abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI)-based models can quantify tumour volume in positron emission tomography (PET) examinations using prostate specific membrane antigen (PSMA). It is, however, unknown whether this measurement of tumour volume contains prognostic information. The purpose of this study was to examine whether tumour volume measured by AI is associated with overall survival in patients with prostate cancer. Methods Patients who had undergone [ 18 F]PSMA-1007 PET-CT due to primary staging or biochemical recurrence (BCR) of prostate cancer at our centre were retrospectively included and followed for 5 years. Automatic quantification of tumour volume was performed using a previously developed fully automated AI model from our research group for PSMA PET-CT analysis, without manual corrections. The tumour volume for the prostate, lymph nodes, and bone was calculated and summarized as Total Lesion Volume (TLV) and divided categorically (no detectable tumour, low, and high) as well as aggregated to whole-body TLV and divided into tertiles (low, intermediate, and high). Mortality rates were compared using Cox-regression and adjusted for age. Results Among 267 patients in the final analysis, 48 (18%) died during follow-up. Whole-body TLV was significantly associated with mortality in the combined cohort (p = 0.001) and in the primary staging cohort (p = 0.014) but did not reach statistical significance in the BCR cohort (p = 0.061). Conclusions Fully automated AI-derived TLV from PSMA PET-CT was associated with overall survival. These findings support the potential role of AI-based tumour quantification as a potential prognostic biomarker in prostate cancer.

title: Bias-Controlled Quantitative Analysis of Golgi-Stained Neurons via High-Fidelity Denoising.
abstract: Quantitative analysis of Golgi-stained neurons is fundamentally limited by non-specific precipitates that introduce substantial bias into morphological measurements. Conventional denoising approaches, designed mainly for low-resolution medical imaging or reconstruction artefacts, are insufficient for suppressing this chemically induced noise at sub-micrometre resolution. Here, we present a high-fidelity denoising strategy for Golgi-stained neurons (HiFi Golgi), a bias-controlled analytical strategy for three-dimensional (3D) Golgi-stained neuronal imaging. We established a multidimensional evaluation framework to systematically quantify the trade-off between noise suppression and structural fidelity, enabling rigorous comparison of candidate filtering strategies. Using this framework, an optimised low-parameter bilateral filter was identified that minimises noise-induced bias while preserving neuronal morphology. The HiFi Golgi strategy consistently reduces bias across diverse brain regions, imaging resolutions, and model species without parameter re-optimization, improving the reliability and reproducibility of single-neuron reconstruction. This work provides a generalizable and high-fidelity analytical approach for bias-controlled volumetric imaging, offering a reproducible framework for quantitative morphological analysis in complex neuronal systems.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Intraoperative Imprint Cytology and Frozen Section in Ovarian Tumours: Experience From a Tertiary Care Centre in Montenegro.
abstract: Objective Intraoperative assessment of ovarian tumours is crucial for surgical decision-making, especially regarding extent of resection and fertility preservation. Frozen section is standard, while imprint cytology is a potential alternative method. The aim was to evaluate and compare the diagnostic accuracy of imprint cytology and frozen section in ovarian tumours using final histopathology as the reference standard in this study. Methods This retrospective study included 29 consecutive patients with ovarian masses operated at a tertiary care centre in Montenegro during 2023-2024. All cases were evaluated intraoperatively using both imprint cytology and frozen section. Final histopathological diagnosis on paraffin-embedded sections, classified according to WHO 2020 criteria, served as reference standard. Archival material was reviewed independently by two pathologists blinded to final diagnosis; discrepancies were resolved by consensus. Statistical analysis included sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, accuracy, and correlation testing using chi-square test and Spearman correlation with p < 0.05 significant. Results Imprint cytology correctly classified 28/29 cases, yielding an overall diagnostic accuracy of 96.6%. Sensitivity was 100% for benign and borderline tumours and 80% for malignant tumours. Frozen section correctly classified 26/29 cases, with an overall accuracy of 89.7%; sensitivity was 100% for benign, 50% for borderline and 60% for malignant tumours. Agreement with final histopathology was higher for imprint cytology (κ = 0.907) than for frozen section (κ = 0.704). The difference in overall accuracy was not statistically significant (McNemar p = 0.500). Conclusion Imprint cytology demonstrated promising diagnostic performance and may represent a useful adjunct or alternative to frozen section, particularly in resource-limited settings. Larger prospective multicentre studies are required to validate these findings.

title: Combination of ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy and phlebectomy in the treatment of the anterior saphenous vein insufficiency - a single-center retrospective study with long-term follow-up.
abstract: Background Isolated insufficiency of the anterior saphenous vein is common and as clinically relevant as the great saphenous vein insufficiency. Data regarding its optimal management are lacking. Patients and methods We retrospectively analyzed data from patients with isolated anterior saphenous vein varicosities who were treated at the Department of Dermatology, University of Lübeck, between 2013 and 2021. All patients underwent combined treatment consisting of ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy of the proximal intrafascial venous segment and phlebectomy of the extrafascial tributaries. The sclerosant was polidocanol. A successful outcome was defined as a combination of successful ablation and the absence of newly developed refluxing tributaries at follow-up. Results 70 patients (56 female, 14 male) were included, with a mean follow-up period of 6.09 years (range: 6 months-10.2 years). The overall success rate was 81.4%. At follow-up, all patients showed an improvement in their clinical class according to the Clinical, Etiological, Anatomical, and Pathophysiological (CEAP) classification (p < 0.001). A significant correlation was found between the volume of polidocanol foam injected and successful sclerotherapy (p < 0.05). Conclusions Combined ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy and phlebectomy is an effective treatment for isolated anterior saphenous vein varicosis, providing long-term success while preserving the great saphenous vein.

title: Early Changes in Peripancreatic Mesenteric Fat Beyond Weight Loss Predict Durability of Hepatic Improvements in MASLD.
abstract: Aims Various visceral adipose tissue depots exhibit heterogeneous metabolic properties. This study aims to explore whether specific abdominal fat compartments differentially predict loss of sustained treatment response to lifestyle interventions in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Materials and methods Consecutive treatment-naïve MASLD patients were prospectively enrolled from January 2015 to March 2024, with a 96-week follow-up period. Liver fat content, preperitoneal fat thickness (PFT), peripancreatic mesenteric fat thickness (MFT1), periumbilical mesenteric fat thickness (MFT2) and perirenal fat thickness (PrFT) were quantified using magnetic resonance imaging. Liver stiffness measurement (LSM) was assessed by 2D-SWE. Treatment responses were evaluated at 48 and 96 weeks, and the primary outcome was loss of response at 96 weeks. Results A total of 631 MASLD patients (mean age: 41.5 ± 13.8 years; 72.0% male) were included. Logistic regression analyses revealed that a greater 48-week relative decrease in MFT1 (per 10% relative reduction), rather than in MFT2, PFT or PrFT, was independently associated with lower odds of losing MRI-PDFF response (OR: 0.48, 95% CI: 0.34-0.69, p < 0.001) and LSM response (OR: 0.53, 95% CI: 0.28-0.99, p = 0.046) at 96 weeks. Receiver operating characteristic curve analyses indicated that relative changes in MFT1 showed discriminatory ability for the loss of MRI-PDFF and LSM responses, with areas under the curves of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.64-0.76) and 0.77 (95% CI: 0.67-0.88), respectively. Conclusions Early changes in MFT1 were associated with subsequent loss of response in hepatic steatosis and fibrosis, suggesting potential prognostic value for hepatic response durability in MASLD.

title: Multimodal Echocardiography for Assessing Left Ventricular Function: Recent Advances and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Background Left ventricular (LV) function occupies a central position in cardiovascular health and disease, and its accurate noninvasive evaluation has accordingly attracted sustained investigative interest. In recent years, a succession of emerging echocardiographic techniques has expanded the scope of LV function evaluation beyond conventional volumetric parameters. These advances collectively enable a multidimensional characterization of cardiac anatomy, mechanics, perfusion, and microcirculation. Within this evolving paradigm, multimodal echocardiography represents a promising framework for comprehensive evaluation of LV function and forms the subject of the present review. Scope and approach This review summarizes the principles and recent advances of three-dimensional echocardiography (3DE), speckle tracking echocardiography (STE), contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), and super-resolution ultrasound (SRUS) in LV function assessment, together with their representative clinical applications, the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI) in multimodal fusion, and the translational challenges toward clinical practice. Key findings and conclusions Current evidence indicates that these techniques extend LV function assessment beyond conventional parameters, affording geometry-independent volumetric quantification, sensitive detection of subclinical myocardial dysfunction, quantitative evaluation of microcirculatory perfusion, and direct visualization of myocardial microvessels. These technologies span a spectrum of validation and clinical adoption, ranging from established applications recommended for routine use in guidelines, through selected specialist applications, to experimental approaches that remain at the stage of feasibility validation or conceptual design. Although operator dependence, cross-platform variability, and the absence of standardized protocols remain major barriers to the routine application of the latter two categories of technologies, the complementarity of these modalities yields mechanistic and prognostic insights that no single technique can provide in isolation. Continued advances must be matched by validation in large-scale, multicenter, prospective studies. Only then can multimodal echocardiography deliver the noninvasive, multiscale, and integrated assessment of LV function.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Echocardiographic Platform for Automated Measurements in Children.
abstract: Purpose This study assessed the accuracy of a novel artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted echocardiographic platform for automated measurements in children. Methods In this prospective, blinded, comparative, single-center pilot study, transthoracic echocardiography was performed in pediatric subjects aged 5 to 18 years using the Siemens Acuson Origin cardiovascular ultrasound system. For spectral Doppler assessments, two echocardiographic acquisitions were required: one using the AI-assisted protocol with automatic spectral Doppler marker placement, and one with manual marker placement. For all other analyses, a single manual acquisition was required for subsequent AI and manual assessments. Images were initially analyzed with the AI-assisted protocol, followed immediately by manual evaluation by a pediatric cardiologist blinded to the AI-derived results. Indices included B-mode, M-mode, Doppler, speckle tracking, and four-dimensional (4D) parameters. Agreement between AI-assisted and manual measurements was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis. Results Thirty subjects (23 males; age 12.2±3.8 years) were studied, including 23 with structurally normal heart, six with congenital heart diseases, and one with dilated cardiomyopathy. Feasibility exceeded 90% for 2D AI-assisted assessment and 80% for 4D ventricular volumetry, but was below 35% for 4D atrial volumetry. Agreement between AI-assisted and manual measurements was strong for all parameters except septal (ICC 0.2) and left ventricular posterior wall thickness (ICC 0.5). Bland-Altman analysis showed no significant systematic differences. Conclusion Our pilot findings suggest that a commercially available AI-assisted echocardiographic system may be feasible and reasonably accurate for conventional and advanced quantitative echocardiographic assessment for children in a real-world setting.

title: Cognitive Cerebellum Structure and Functional Connectivity in Relation to Executive Functions in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.
abstract: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) has been primarily linked to abnormalities within the cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuit; however, recent evidence suggests that the posterior cerebellum may contribute to the executive dysfunction observed in the disorder. In 56 adults (28 OCD, 28 controls), we assessed executive functions using the BANFE-2 battery and integrated structural MRI (T1) and resting-state fMRI. Although the Global Executive Index did not differ significantly between groups, patients with OCD showed significantly lower scores in the inhibitory control/decision-making domain relative to controls. We quantified cortical thickness and volume (% intracranial volume) in Crus I/II and lobule VI using CERES and examined resting-state functional connectivity (seed-to-voxel) in CONN, adjusting for age, sex, medication, and depression. Compared with controls, patients with OCD showed reduced bilateral cortical thickness in Crus I/II and lobule VI (false discovery rate-corrected q < 0.05; β_OCD - Control = -0.27 to -0.59; ηp 2 = 0.34-0.55), with no significant volumetric differences after correction for multiple comparisons. Functional connectivity results revealed a mixed pattern, including focal hyperconnectivity (e.g., left Crus I with primary auditory cortex; left Crus II with occipital cortex) and widespread intracerebellar hypoconnectivity. In addition, significant Group × executive-function interactions (p-family-wise error < 0.05) emerged mainly for bilateral Crus I (Global Executive Index and working memory/flexibility) and left lobule VI (inhibition/decision-making), indicating that the relationship between cerebellar connectivity and executive performance differs in OCD relative to controls. These findings support an expanded model of executive circuits in OCD that incorporates the posterior cerebellum as a relevant node.

title: Convergence of Cerebrospinal Fluid Neuronal Biomarker Burden and MRI Lesion Pattern and Its Association With Short-Term Outcome in Neuroinfectious Diseases.
abstract: Background Neuroinfectious diseases (NDs) are potentially treatable conditions associated with substantial morbidity, but their clinical course remains difficult to predict. While specific MRI patterns are characteristic of distinct aetiologies, their prognostic value remains poorly investigated. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers of neuroaxonal and synaptic damage have been linked to clinical outcome. We investigated the association of CSF biomarkers and MRI findings with short-term outcome in NDs. Methods In this multicentre cohort study, CSF was analysed in 123 patients with NDs and in 95 non-neuroinflammatory controls. Concentrations of beta-synuclein, SNAP-25, neurogranin and neurofilament light chain protein (NfL) were measured. MRI findings were classified by topography and lesion pattern. Clinical outcome at discharge was assessed using the modified Rankin Scale and degree of recovery. Results All CSF biomarkers were higher in ND patients with MRI abnormalities than in those without MRI abnormalities and/or controls, also within the (meningo-)encephalitis group. Temporal lobe involvement was the MRI pattern most consistently associated with elevated CSF biomarkers, even after multivariable adjustment including aetiology, and was independently associated with poor functional outcome and incomplete recovery. A global neuronal biomarker burden derived by principal component analysis (PC1) improved the fit of outcome models including MRI lesion pattern, with both temporal lobe involvement and PC1 remaining independently associated with outcome at discharge. Conclusions MRI lesion pattern and CSF biomarkers of synaptic and neuroaxonal damage were independently associated with short-term outcome in NDs, suggesting that they capture complementary aspects of disease severity. Prospective studies are needed to establish their prognostic value.

title: The CoMPaSS-NMD Atlas Platform: A Secure Multimodal Infrastructure for Harmonized Data Collection, Exploration, and Future Artificial Intelligence-Driven Stratification in Hereditary Neuromuscular Disorders.
abstract: Background Hereditary neuromuscular disorders exhibit marked phenotypic and molecular heterogeneity, which weakens genotype-phenotype correlation and complicates timely diagnosis, prognosis, and patient stratification for clinical trials. The Horizon Europe project CoMPaSS-NMD aims to develop artificial-intelligence-based stratification tools by integrating clinical, genetic, histopathological, and imaging data from clinical reference centers across Europe and the United Kingdom. Methods We developed CoMPaSS-NMD Atlas, a secure, modular web platform for pseudonymized data collection, multimodal data management, and controlled exploration. Clinical, technical, and data-management experts defined requirements; contributing centers co-designed electronic clinical and histopathology forms. Clinical phenotypes used the Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO), while imaging, histopathology, and sequencing data followed international standards. Results The platform supports role- and attribute-based access, pseudonymized patient registration, metadata management, structured clinical data entry, MRI and histopathological uploads, and a dedicated genetic-sequencing workflow. Cohort-level exploration is driven by structured metadata and HPO terms, enabling hierarchical phenotype navigation, ontology-aware data navigation, and cross-domain queries spanning clinical, genetic, imaging, and histopathological features. Users can download raw files in their original formats, along with structured metadata reports in CSV or PDF, according to the permissions defined for data protection. Conclusions The Atlas provides a foundation for harmonized, standardized prospective data collection and for building large datasets for artificial intelligence- and machine learning-based patient stratification. With secure governance, traceability, and multimodal integration, it is designed to support diagnostic and stratification research in hereditary neuromuscular disorders; clinical validation is ongoing.

title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to conventional oral photographs for recognition, classification, localization, segmentation, and risk assessment of oral mucosal lesions. This systematic review evaluated how clinically relevant visual information-including color, texture, morphology, borders, and spatial patterns-is represented by AI systems and assessed performance, validation, explainability, human comparison, and clinical translation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for studies directly analyzing conventional white-light clinical photographs. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation-based approaches. Fifty-three studies were included, 30 published in 2025-2026. Forty-six used implicit deep-learning visual representations, three multimodal vision-language models, two explicit color analyses, and two explicit texture analyses. Thirty-one studies primarily addressed image-level diagnostic classification/recognition, 15 spatial detection/localization or lesion delineation, six screening/triage/referral or biopsy-oriented decision support, and one longitudinal malignant-transformation prediction. Six used independent external cohorts and five compared AI with human readers. Methodological concerns were frequent, no sufficiently coherent group supported meta-analysis, and certainty remained limited across evidence bodies. Current evidence therefore supports technical feasibility rather than established clinical effectiveness, with translation requiring stronger patient-level independence, external validation, prospective multicenter evaluation, and evidence of clinical benefit.

title: CDKN1A Mediates Regulated Cell Death in Osteoblasts and Exacerbates Periapical Bone Destruction in Apical Periodontitis.
abstract: Background Apical periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory bone-destructive disease driven by intracanal microbial infection and host immune-inflammatory responses. Periapical bone destruction arises not only from excessive osteoclastic resorption but also from osteoblast dysfunction and dysregulated regulated cell death (RCD). CDKN1A (p21) is a canonical cell-cycle regulator implicated in multiple RCD programs, yet its role in osteoblast injury and apical periodontitis pathogenesis remains undefined. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing (ScRNA) was used to profile osteoblast subpopulations and RCD-related gene expression in human periapical lesions. Porphyromonas gingivalis infection models were established in MG63 and MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts, and DIA proteomics and western blot were used to evaluate RCD-related proteins. The effects of CDKN1A, a disease-associated hub gene screened out in DIA proteomics, on RCD-related proteins were further examined by western blot. Lentiviral silencing and AAV-mediated overexpression were performed in vitro and in rat apical periodontitis models. Bone destruction, RCD activation and osteogenic capacity were assessed by micro-CT, histomorphology and multiplex immunofluorescence. CDKN1A (p21) is a canonical cell-cycle regulator implicated in multiple RCD programs, yet its role in osteoblast injury and apical periodontitis pathogenesis remains undefined.

Porphyromonas gingivalis infection models were established in MG63 and MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts, and DIA proteomics and western blot were used to evaluate RCD-related proteins. Lentiviral silencing and AAV-mediated overexpression were performed in vitro and in rat apical periodontitis models. ScRNA data of apical periodontitis showed that osteoblasts in apical lesions exhibited enhanced apoptosis and pyroptosis and reduced ferroptosis. Single-bacteria P. gingivalis infection markedly upregulated CDKN1A, which promoted osteoblast apoptosis and pyroptosis while suppressing necroptosis and ferroptosis. In vivo, CDKN1A expression increased with disease progression and was negatively correlated with the osteogenic marker OPN. CDKN1A overexpression aggravated bone destruction, whereas its knockdown significantly attenuated bone loss and restored osteogenic activity.

Conclusion

CDKN1A acts as a critical regulator that mediates RCD of osteoblasts, impairs osteogenesis and exacerbates periapical bone destruction in apical periodontitis. title: Clinical Diagnosis Versus Plain Radiography for Diabetic Foot Osteomyelitis: A Prospective Study of Diagnostic Agreement in a Resource-Limited Settings.
abstract: Diabetic foot osteomyelitis (DFO) is a serious complication of diabetic foot ulcers, particularly in advanced infections. In low-resource settings, access to medical imaging may be limited. This study evaluated the diagnostic agreement between a composite clinical approach (clinical assessment plus probe-to-bone test) compared with plain radiography for diagnosing DFO, including performance across ulcer categories. A prospective cohort study was conducted from December 2021 to January 2025 among patients with suspected DFO. Participants underwent clinical evaluation, risk factor assessment, ulcer history, SINBAD classification, probe-to-bone testing and plain radiography. Diagnostic performance measures were calculated. Given the absence of a gold standard reference test (bone biopsy) in this low-resource setting, performance measures represent comparative diagnostic agreement with plain radiography rather than absolute diagnostic accuracy. A total of 166 patients with deep foot ulcers were enrolled. Composite clinical diagnosis identified osteomyelitis in 117 patients and excluded it in 49. Plain radiography was positive in 96 of 117 composite positive cases, while 21 were discordant; all 49 composite negative cases were radiographically negative. The composite approach showed 100% sensitivity, 70% specificity and 87.3% overall agreement. Sensitivity remained 100% across ulcer categories, while specificity increased significantly from 63.8% in SINBAD-4 ulcers to 77.8% in SINBAD-5 ulcers, improving agreement from 86.1% to 89.7%. In conclusion, composite clinical diagnosis demonstrates substantial agreement with plain radiography in this cohort of patients with suspected DFO. This can provide a practical adjunct for clinical assessment in resource-limited settings where imaging is unavailable or difficult to interpret but should not be considered a definitive diagnostic test in the absence of an independent reference standard.
