title: Preoperative Risk Stratification of Lymph Node Metastasis in cT1 Lung Adenocarcinoma Using CT Radiomics and Habitat Analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate preoperative assessment of lymph node metastasis (LNM) is important for risk stratification and surgical planning in patients with cT1 lung adenocarcinoma. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a multi-regional computed tomography (CT) radiomics model incorporating intratumoral, peritumoral, and habitat information for preoperative prediction of LNM. Methods A total of 172 patients with cT1 invasive lung adenocarcinoma from one institution were retrospectively included and randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 120) and an internal validation cohort (n = 52). An independent cohort of 63 patients from a second institution was used for external validation. Radiomic features were extracted from the intratumoral region, a 3-mm peritumoral region, and two habitat subregions generated using K-means clustering. After feature selection, a multi-regional radiomic signature (Radscore) was constructed and combined with preoperative clinical variables using logistic regression. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV). Results Nineteen radiomic features were retained in the final radiomic signature. In the internal validation cohort, the clinical, radiomic, and combined models achieved AUCs of 0.758, 0.844, and 0.852, respectively. Using a prespecified training-derived threshold of 0.4036, the combined model achieved a sensitivity of 65.0%, specificity of 87.5%, and NPV of 80.0% in the internal validation cohort. In the independent external cohort, the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.837 (95% CI: 0.731–0.930), with an accuracy of 77.8%, sensitivity of 77.3%, specificity of 78.0%, PPV of 65.4%, and NPV of 86.5%. The Radscore was significantly associated with IASLC pathological grade and visceral pleural invasion (both P < 0.001). Conclusions The multi-regional CT radiomics model incorporating intratumoral, peritumoral, and habitat information demonstrated good discrimination for preoperative LNM risk stratification in cT1 lung adenocarcinoma and maintained stable performance in an independent external cohort. The model may provide complementary quantitative information for preoperative risk assessment, although further prospective validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

title: Hierarchical transfer learning and region of interest standardization for bone age assessment in Thai children
abstract: Abstract \normalfont\unboldmath Bone age assessment (BAA) from hand radiographs is routinely used to evaluate child growth and endocrine disorders, but manual atlas-based reading is slow and reader-dependent, while deep learning models trained on large international datasets may lose accuracy in other populations. We developed a population-specific AI framework for BAA in Thai children. It combines ROI standardization using contrast enhancement, automatic hand detection, and segmentation with an EfficientNetB7 regression model trained through hierarchical transfer learning. The model first learned skeletal-maturity representations from the public RSNA and DHA datasets and was then fine-tuned on Thai hospital data. On a held-out Thai test set excluded from BAA training and validation, hierarchical adaptation achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.64 months (RMSE, 5.85 months; \((R^2=0.98)\)), compared with 5.73 months for pooled training and 7.60 months for the public-only baseline. The full preprocessing pipeline also reduced downstream MAE relative to raw radiographs. It met the predefined detection-and-segmentation processing criterion for all evaluated RSNA and DHA images; however, this finding represents processing completeness rather than independent quantitative validation of segmentation accuracy. Among GP, TW, and a hybrid strategy using TW when applicable and GP outside the validated TW3-RUS range, the hybrid produced the lowest point-estimate MAE, although its advantage over TW was small. Grad-CAM provided exploratory evidence of attention to anatomically relevant regions but also identified localized or non-skeletal attention. Improved RSNA hand ROI annotations are released to support future research.

title: Hypervascular anterior mediastinal hyaline vascular-type Castleman disease with a feeding-vessel sign and intraoperative arterial bleeding: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Hyaline vascular-type Castleman disease is characterized by prominent vascular proliferation. When it occurs in the anterior mediastinum, its location and morphology may overlap with thymic tumors. Recognizing a hypervascular phenotype before minimally invasive resection is clinically important because unexpected arterial bleeding can complicate surgery. Case presentation: A 35-year-old man without constitutional or inflammatory symptoms was incidentally found to have a well-circumscribed left anterior mediastinal soft-tissue mass measuring approximately 49 × 25 mm. Mean attenuation increased from approximately 46 Hounsfield units (HU) on unenhanced computed tomography (CT) to 121 HU in the arterial phase (ΔHU ≈ 75 HU), with persistent delayed enhancement. Serial review of arterial-phase CT images suggested a feeding branch arising from the internal thoracic artery. On 3.0-T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), the lesion was isointense on T1-weighted images and relatively hyperintense on T2-weighted images; diffusion-weighted imaging showed no definite high signal, whereas dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI demonstrated marked arterial enhancement with persistent delayed enhancement. Complete resection was achieved by single-port video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery. Bleeding from a mediastinal arterial branch occurred during dissection and was controlled intraoperatively. Histopathologic and immunohistochemical findings supported hyaline vascular-type Castleman disease. Follow-up noncontrast CT approximately 26 months after surgery showed no definite local recurrence. Conclusions In a well-circumscribed anterior mediastinal mass, disproportionate arterial enhancement, a traceable feeding vessel, and persistent enhancement should raise suspicion for a hypervascular lesion and prompt deliberate planning for vascular control. These findings are not specific for Castleman disease, and definitive diagnosis remains histopathologic, but preoperative recognition of hypervascularity may reduce avoidable surgical risk.

title: Development and internal validation of a multivariable logistic model for pulp disease in children from the central Peruvian Amazon: a secondary analysis of a case–control study
abstract: Abstract Background Pulp disease is a frequent and largely preventable consequence of untreated dental caries in children, yet its determinants are seldom modelled jointly in socioeconomically vulnerable settings, and probability models that could support screening in primary care are rarely developed or validated. We aimed to identify factors independently associated with pulp disease and to develop and internally validate a multivariable logistic model estimating its probability in children from the central Peruvian Amazon. Methods This was a secondary analysis of the individual-level dataset of a case–control study conducted in 2023 at the primary health care centre of Pichanaki (Chanchamayo, Junín, Peru), comprising 270 children aged 5 to 11 years: 90 cases with pulpal or periapical pathology diagnosed on clinical and radiographic grounds and 180 controls without pulpal involvement. Biological (anemia, hemoglobin concentration, nutritional status), behavioural (fluoride toothpaste, mouthwash and dental floss use, ferrous sulfate intake) and socioeconomic variables (maternal educational level and occupation, maternal age, household income) were retrieved from a previously collected and validated database. Variables with p < 0.20 in bivariable analysis, together with clinically relevant covariates, were entered into a multivariable binary logistic regression model; multicollinearity was assessed with the variance inflation factor. Discrimination was quantified with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration with the Hosmer–Lemeshow test and a calibration curve, and internal validity with a 70/30 training–test split and k-fold cross-validation. The optimal classification threshold was derived from the Youden index, and performance was re-estimated across alternative thresholds. title: Third ventricle width on routine MRI is associated with processing speed in multiple sclerosis: a single-centre retrospective observational study
abstract: Abstract Background: Cognitive impairment is common in multiple sclerosis (MS), and slowed information processing is among its most frequent manifestations. Although brain volumetry can quantify atrophy, automated volumetric tools are not universally available in routine practice. We investigated whether third ventricle width (3VW), a simple linear measure obtainable on conventional MRI, is associated with standardised Symbol Digit Modalities Test performance. Methods: This single-centre retrospective observational study included 100 adults with MS assessed in routine care between 2021 and 2023. Current MRI was acquired within one month of cognitive testing. A neuroradiologist blinded to cognitive results measured 3VW three times at the foramen of Monro, and the mean value was analysed. The primary analysis examined the association between current 3VW and age-standardised SDMT performance (SDMT-SD) using Spearman correlation with false-discovery-rate correction. Post hoc multivariable linear-regression sensitivity analyses adjusted for demographic and clinical covariates. MRI measurements approximately 3, 5 and 10 years earlier and analyses of SDMT impairment were exploratory. Results: Twenty-five participants (25%) met the prespecified definition of SDMT impairment (SDMT-SD ≤ -1). Current 3VW was inversely associated with SDMT-SD (rho = -0.556, 95% CI -0.678 to -0.404; q = 2.28 × 10⁻⁸). The association persisted in a fully adjusted linear-regression sensitivity model including age, sex, education and EDSS (β = -0.232 SDMT-SD units per 1-mm greater 3VW, 95% CI -0.391 to -0.074; p = 0.0045). Excluding 14 records previously labelled as CIS produced similar results. Analyses of prior MRI showed associations in selected subgroups but were limited by non-random availability of earlier scans. Conclusions: Greater third ventricle width on routine MRI is associated with worse processing-speed performance in MS. Because it is rapid to obtain and widely accessible, 3VW may serve as a simple imaging marker that prompts cognitive assessment when volumetric tools are unavailable. It should not replace cognitive testing or volumetric MRI, and predictive thresholds require prospective external validation.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Imprint Cytology in Sentinel Lymph Node Evaluation of Breast Cancer Patients in a Resource-Limited Setting
abstract: Abstract Background Sentinel lymph node biopsy is a standard technique for staging of breast node-negative axilla in patients undergoing a mastectomy or breast-conserving surgery. Evidence on touch imprint cytology performance from resource-limited settings, which depends solely on a single technique, is comparatively limited. The study aimed to test the sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of touch imprint cytology and compare it with final histopathology as a reference standard. Methods The study was a retrospective observational study among 88 breast cancer patients who underwent mastectomy or breast-conserving surgery over two years. Following intraoperative imprint cytology of sentinel lymph nodes, results were communicated to the operating surgeon, who then proceeded with definitive surgery, lumpectomy or mastectomy with or without axillary dissection. Excised specimens were subsequently sent for formal histopathological analysis. A set of diagnostic performance indicators, such as sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and general accuracy, was determined. Results The sensitivity and specificity were found to be 93.8% and 75.0%, respectively. The median number of lymph nodes evaluated per case was 3(IQR: 2, range: 1 to 7). The positive and negative predictive values were 45.5% and 98.2%, respectively; overall accuracy was 78.4%, and all estimates were given with 95% confidence limits, highlighting the reliability of the findings. Conclusions Touch imprint cytology demonstrated high sensitivity and a clinically meaningful NPV value in this study, supporting its use as a primary intraoperative technique where frozen sections were unavailable. Nonetheless, false negative results remain a concern, as they can cause under-treatment and require completion of axillary dissection.

title: Value of ultrasound in diagnosis and treatment of Guillain-Barre syndrome
abstract: Abstract Objective This study aimed to evaluate the clinical value of high-frequency ultrasound in the early diagnosis of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) by observing morphological alterations in peripheral nerves. We further summarized the characteristic ultrasonographic changes of peripheral nerves during clinical treatment and explored the feasibility of ultrasound for prognostic evaluation in patients with GBS. Methods 35 GBS patients were selected as the experimental group. High-frequency ultrasonic examinations of their peripheral nerves were performed at the time of admission, 7 days (n = 35), 1 month (n = 34), and 6 months (n = 30) after treatment, respectively. The results were compared with those of the control group to summarize the changing patterns, and the patients with poor prognosis were analyzed at the same time. Result At admission, the cross-sectional area (CSA) values of the C5 and C6 nerve roots, median nerve (wrist, elbow, and axillary segments), ulnar nerve (wrist, elbow, and axillary segments), sciatic nerve, tibial nerve, peroneal nerve, and sural nerve were significantly increased in GBS patients compared with the control group (all P < 0.05). At 6 months after treatment, among patients with a Hughes functional score greater than 3, the CSA of the C5 nerve root, axillary median nerve, and axillary ulnar nerve remained remarkably larger than that in the control group, and the differences were statistically significant (P < 0.05). Conclusion Persistent thickening of the C5 nerve root, axillary median nerve, and axillary ulnar nerve at the 6-month follow-up may serve as independent adverse prognostic indicators for patients with GBS.

title: Two-Phase Transfer Learning for Automated Measurement and Severity Grading of Scoliosis and Spondylolisthesis on Spinal Radiographs
abstract: Abstract Background Cobb angle and vertebral slip measurements are clinically vali-dated techniques that are time-intensive and prone to inter-observer variation. Objective To develop a comprehensive deep learning approach for auto-mated measurements and grading of scoliosis and spondylolisthesis cases using a single-center hospital radiograph dataset. Methods In this retrospective study, 2,500 anonymized spinal radiographs from one participating hospital were used, including 1,635 scoliosis and 865 spondy-lolisthesis radiographs. Researchers had access only to radiographs without any patient identifiers, demographic information, and clinical data. Radiographs were preprocessed by applying Gaussian denoising, CLAHE contrast adjust-ment, intensity standardization, and scaling to 224 x 224 pixels. Vertebral landmark-based vertebral angles were computed for scoliosis analysis, and verte-bral body localization-based slip percentages were calculated for spondylolisthesis detection. Two networks, DenseNet201, and ResNet152, were fine-tuned with two-stage ImageNet transfer learning approach. Results DenseNet201 obtained an accuracy of 87.5% for scoliosis and 88.4% for spondylolisthesis on hold-out test subsets. Cobb-angle MAE was 1.845° and slip percentage MAE was 1.8 percentage point. The corresponding ICC values were 0.962 and 0.958, and macro-AUC values were 0.83 and 0.84. Conclusion The proposed method demonstrated strong internal validity in terms of spinal deformity measurement and grading within the context of a single-center study. Since patient matching was not possible, patient-level independence of the image split could not be confirmed. These results, therefore, constitute internal validation at the level of the image and need to be externally validated independently. Clinical trial registration Not applicable. This study was retrospective and did not involve a clinical trial or prospective intervention.

title: Dynamic Graph and Multi-Stage Mamba Fusion for Multimodal Survival Prediction
abstract: Abstract Multimodal survival prediction using whole-slide images (WSIs) and genomic profiles is important for cancer prognosis; however, integrating gigapixel histopathology with high-dimensional molecular data remains challenging. Existing methods often rely on dense or fixed fusion strategies that may introduce redundant interactions and inadequately capture patient-specific pathology--molecular associations. We propose a sample-adaptive WSI-omics framework that constructs sparse pathway--patch interactions and combines graph-based refinement with selective state-space aggregation for patient-level survival prediction. The framework was evaluated on five TCGA cohorts using patient-level 5-fold cross-validation. Compared with SurvPath, the proposed method improved the average C-index from 0.609 to 0.638, corresponding to an absolute gain of 0.029. The improvement reached significance only in BLCA under the paired \((t)\)-test, indicating cohort-dependent statistical support. Matched profiling showed lower memory consumption than the Transformer replacement, while case-level visualizations provided model-derived pathway--patch associations. These results support sample-adaptive sparse interaction modeling for WSI-omics survival prediction. External validation, repeated-seed evaluation, and pathologist-guided interpretation remain necessary before clinical application.

title: Selective Endometrial Screening versus Routine Curettage in Postmenopausal Women Undergoing Intrauterine Device Removal: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background The choice between selective and routine endometrial screening during postmenopausal intrauterine device (IUD) removal remains controversial. Universal blind curettage frequently yields insufficient endometrial tissue and results in overtreatment. This study aimed to evaluate a selective, risk-stratified endometrial screening strategy for postmenopausal women undergoing IUD removal and develop an individualized endometrial screening strategy for this patient population. Methods A total of 512 naturally postmenopausal women (amenorrhea ≥ 12 months) who underwent IUD removal were retrospectively enrolled. According to the presence or absence of postmenopausal abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB), patients were divided into a bleeding group (n = 128) and a non-bleeding group (n = 384). All patients with AUB underwent endometrial sampling; asymptomatic patients were sampled only when high-risk transvaginal ultrasound findings were present (endometrial thickness > 8 mm, heterogeneous echogenicity, or uterine cavity effusion; n = 218). The remaining 166 low-risk asymptomatic patients underwent IUD removal alone. Baseline clinical characteristics, preoperative transvaginal ultrasound findings, and postoperative pathological outcomes were analyzed. Results Patients with AUB had significantly higher body mass index (BMI), higher prevalence of diabetes mellitus, hormone replacement therapy (HRT) history, and tamoxifen exposure history (all P < 0.05). Endometrial thickening, heterogeneous echogenicity, and uterine cavity effusion were all significantly more common in the AUB group (all P < 0.001), whereas the rate of IUD incarceration did not differ (P = 0.121). Among the 346 sampled patients, the overall detection rate of significant endometrial lesions (hyperplasia with or without atypia and carcinoma) was 10.40%. The lesion detection rate in the bleeding group was 14.06%, which was significantly higher than 8.26% in the asymptomatic ultrasound high-risk group (P = 0.040). Low-risk asymptomatic patients with normal ultrasound presented an extremely low risk of severe endometrial lesions. Blind curettage yielded invalid tissue specimens in a proportion of cases. Conclusions Postmenopausal abnormal uterine bleeding, abnormal endometrial ultrasound features, diabetes, obesity, and hormone-related exposure are significant risk factors for endometrial lesions in postmenopausal women undergoing IUD removal. Routine universal curettage is unnecessary for unselected postmenopausal women undergoing IUD removal. A selective endometrial screening strategy integrating clinical symptoms, transvaginal ultrasound and systemic risk factors is feasible, safe and effective. It avoids unnecessary curettage in around one-third of patients and reduces overtreatment.

title: CompDiff enables fair and zero shot medical image generation across demographic intersections through compositional diffusion
abstract: Abstract Medical image generators trained on imbalanced data can fail at demographic intersections absent from training. We introduce CompDiff, which encodes age, sex and race separately and composes supervised demographic tokens alongside clinical text. Across chest radiographs and fundus images, CompDiff improves overall and subgroup fidelity relative to prompt conditioning (RoentGen-v2) and loss reweighting (FairDiffusion). It generalises in zero-shot generation to 16 chest X-ray intersections excluded from training, achieving the lowest mean FID-RadImageNet in every intersection. In a blinded reader study of these unseen intersections, two radiologists gave CompDiff the highest mean scores among generators for anatomical realism and agreement with the clinical impression, and selected its images most often as the most realistic. Pretraining with CompDiff images improved downstream classification, while CompDiff audit cohorts reduced estimation error on rare intersections. These findings support compositional demographic conditioning for extending medical image synthesis to underserved populations.

title: Noncontrast Multiparametric MRI Adds Value to Preoperative Peritoneal Cancer Index Assessment in Pseudomyxoma Peritonei: Comparison with Contrast-enhanced CT
abstract: Abstract Purpose To compare noncontrast multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) and contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) for agreement with intraoperative peritoneal cancer index (PCI) and detection of key imaging features in pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP). Materials and Methods This retrospective study included 40 patients with pathologically confirmed PMP who underwent cytoreductive surgery and preoperative mpMRI and CECT in 2024. Intraoperative PCI across 13 abdominopelvic regions served as the reference standard. Total PCI agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and Bland–Altman 95% limits of agreement (LoA), with analyses stratified by PCI (≤ 20 vs > 20). Regional agreement and sensitivities for key imaging features were also compared. Results Forty patients (median age, 60 years; 25 women) were included. mpMRI showed greater agreement with intraoperative total PCI than CECT (ICC, 0.98 vs 0.90; difference, 0.08 [95% CI: 0.05, 0.15]), with narrower LoA (7.1 vs 19.1 points). Agreement remained greater with mpMRI for PCI ≤ 20 (ICC, 0.91 vs 0.58) and PCI > 20 (ICC, 0.95 vs 0.74). mpMRI showed higher regional agreement in 11 of 13 regions after multiple-comparison correction. mpMRI had higher sensitivity for mucinous ascites (100% vs 61%; P = 0.002) and intralesional septation (95% vs 37%; P = 0.002), whereas CECT had higher sensitivity for intralesional calcification (100% vs 0%; P = 0.021). Conclusion Noncontrast mpMRI showed greater agreement with intraoperative PCI than CECT and higher sensitivity for mucinous ascites and intralesional septation, whereas CECT better detected intralesional calcification.

Conclusion Noncontrast mpMRI showed greater agreement with intraoperative PCI than CECT and higher sensitivity for mucinous ascites and intralesional septation, whereas CECT better detected intralesional calcification.

title: Chemical Composition of Radiolucent Urinary Stones: A Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy Study
abstract: Abstract Background Radiolucent urinary stones are commonly presumed to represent uric acid calculi; however, the chemical composition of these stones may be heterogeneous. Accurate characterization of stone composition may provide clinically relevant information for understanding stone pathogenesis and optimizing individualized management. This study aimed to determine the FTIR-based chemical composition of radiolucent urinary stones and evaluate its association with demographic and clinical characteristics. Methods This cross-sectional study included 43 patients with radiolucent urinary stones who underwent percutaneous nephrolithotomy or endoscopic lithotripsy at Razi Hospital, Rasht, Iran. Retrieved stones were analyzed using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). Stone composition was classified based on comparison of overall spectral patterns with reference spectra. Associations between stone composition and demographic characteristics, body mass index, stone size, medical history, dietary pattern, urine culture results, and history of urinary tract infection were assessed. Results Mixed stone compositions were identified in 60.5% of specimens, while pure uric acid stones accounted for 14.0%. The most frequent FTIR-based classification was uric acid plus calcium phosphate (53.5%), followed by pure calcium oxalate (25.6%). Overall, uric acid-containing compositions were identified in 74.4% of specimens. Age was significantly associated with stone composition (p = 0.048), with uric acid plus calcium phosphate becoming more frequent among older patients. No significant associations were observed between stone composition and sex, BMI, stone size, previous medical history, dietary pattern, urine culture results, or history of urinary tract infection. Conclusion Radiolucent urinary stones in this cohort demonstrated substantial compositional heterogeneity and should not be assumed to represent pure uric acid stones based solely on radiographic appearance. FTIR analysis identified frequent uric acid-containing mixed compositions, particularly uric acid plus calcium phosphate. These findings highlight the value of direct stone composition assessment in radiolucent calculi and support further investigation using larger cohorts with detailed metabolic evaluation to clarify the mechanisms underlying mixed stone formation.

title: A MobileNetV2-Based Boundary-Aware Improved DeepLabv3+ Network for Gastrointestinal Endoscopic Lesion Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Objective: Gastrointestinal endoscopic lesion segmentation is challenging because lesions often exhibit substantial variations in morphology and size, blurred boundaries, small foreground regions, and complex mucosal background interference. This study proposed an improved DeepLabv3+ segmentation model that integrates a lightweight backbone, cascaded multi-scale contextual modeling, and boundary-aware auxiliary supervision to improve automatic lesion segmentation in endoscopic images. Methods: DeepLabv3+ was used as the baseline framework. The original feature extraction backbone was replaced with MobileNetV2 to reduce model complexity while extracting both low-level spatial details and high-level semantic features. The ASPP module was redesigned as a cascaded multi-scale atrous convolution module to enable feature reuse among branches with different dilation rates. In the low-level feature pathway, a boundary attention module was introduced to enhance contour-related responses according to a predicted boundary probability map. During training, boundary targets were automatically generated from ground-truth masks, and the model was optimized using a combination of cross-entropy loss, Dice loss, and boundary BCE loss. The dataset included 1,445 gastrointestinal endoscopic images with pixel-level labels, of which 1,300 were used for training and 145 for testing. F1-score, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and IoU were used for evaluation. Results: The complete model achieved an F1-score of 0.878, sensitivity of 0.860, specificity of 0.995, accuracy of 0.990, and IoU of 0.784 on the test set. Compared with the original DeepLabv3+ baseline, IoU increased from 0.755 to 0.784. Compared with SegNet, the best-performing competing model, the proposed model improved IoU by 0.040. Ablation experiments demonstrated that both the cascaded ASPP module and the boundary attention branch contributed to performance improvement. Conclusion: The proposed improved DeepLabv3+ model effectively integrates multi-scale semantic information and low-level boundary details, achieving favorable segmentation performance for gastrointestinal endoscopic lesions. This method has potential value for lesion localization, contour delineation, and quantitative analysis in computer-assisted endoscopy.

title: The prognostic role of lateral pelvic lymph nodes in patients with low and mid rectal cancer
abstract: Abstract Purpose Lateral pelvic lymph nodes (LPLNs) represent a potential route of locoregional dissemination in locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). LPLN management remains controversial, with routine LPLN dissection advocated in some Eastern centres, whereas Western strategies rely primarily on neoadjuvant treatment followed by total mesorectal excision (TME) without systematic lateral pelvic lymph node dissection (LPLND). As a result, the prognostic significance of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-suspected LPLNs in patients treated with contemporary neoadjuvant approaches remains uncertain, particularly in Western cohorts where pathological confirmation is rare. This study aimed to determine the incidence of MRI-suspected LPLN involvement and to evaluate its prognostic impact on overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). Methods This was a retrospective study at the Institut Jules Bordet that included patients treated for LARC between January 1, 2007 and December 31, 2021. Pre-treatment MRI was used to identify suspected LPLN involvement. The prognostic impact of MRI-suspected LPLNs on OS and DFS was assessed. Results A total of 115 patients with LARC were included. Twenty-one patients (18.3%) had MRI-suspected LPLNs at diagnosis. Despite a higher risk of LPLN recurrence in the group with MRI-suspected LPLN (9.5% vs 1.1%), no statistically significant association was observed between pre-treatment LPLN status and OS or DFS (P = 0.88 and P = 0.73, respectively). Conclusion In this cohort, MRI-suspected LPLN involvement was not associated with impaired survival outcomes. Prospective studies using standardised radiological criteria and treatment strategies are warranted to better define the prognostic role of LPLNs in LARC.

title: Impact of Epicardial Adipose Tissue on Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Coronary computed tomography Angiography-Based Imaging Analysis
abstract: Abstract Objective This study aimed to explore the association between epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) volume quantified by coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and prognosis in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Patients and methods: In this retrospective study, 119 HFrEF patients undergoing CCTA between January 2022 and December 2023 were enrolled. EAT volume were semi-automatically quantified using CCTA sequences. The primary endpoint was the composite outcome of all-cause mortality and heart failure rehospitalization during follow-up. Cox regression and Kaplan–Meier analyses assessed the association between EAT volume and events. Conventional and time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were used to evaluate predictive performance, and the corresponding areas under the curve (AUC) were calculated. Results Over a median 649-day follow-up, 50 patients (42.0%) experienced endpoint events. Compared with patients without endpoint events, those with endpoints had lower EAT volume (56.55 ± 21.33 cm³ vs. 74.64 ± 25.19 cm³, P < 0.001) and higher EAT density (-72.94 ± 6.80 Hounsfield Units vs. -76.61 ± 5.07 Hounsfield Units, P = 0.002). Multivariate regression analysis showed that EAT volume was an independent prognostic predictor in HFrEF patients; lower EAT volume was associated with poorer prognosis, with a determined cut-off value of 65.53 cm³. Subgroup analysis revealed that patients with lower EAT volume combined with lower body mass index had the poorest prognosis compared with other subgroups. Conclusion In patients with HFrEF, EAT volume is an independent prognostic predictor with moderate predictive value, and its cut-off value may provide additional information for clinical management.

title: Three-dimensional visualisation combined with intraoperative ultrasound in laparoscopic hepatectomy for complex hepatolithiasis: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Objective Complex hepatolithiasis remains challenging for laparoscopic hepatectomy. Three-dimensional visualisation technology (3DVT) alone is limited by its static, preoperative nature, whereas intraoperative ultrasound (IOUS) lacks a global anatomical overview, and quantitative evidence for their synergistic benefit remains insufficient. This propensity score-matched (PSM) retrospective cohort study evaluated whether combined 3DVT and IOUS navigation improves perioperative safety and long-term outcomes compared with conventional two-dimensional imaging in patients with complex hepatolithiasis. Results Among 180 patients who underwent laparoscopic hepatectomy between January 2020 and December 2025, 66 matched pairs were analysed. The combined-navigation group had significantly shorter operative time, less intraoperative blood loss and lower conversion and transfusion rates than the control group (all P < 0.05). The one-stage stone clearance rate was 100.0% versus 90.9% (P = 0.028), and the overall postoperative complication rate was 3.0% versus 18.2% (P = 0.009). Over a mean follow-up of approximately 37 months, the stone recurrence rate was 1.5% versus 10.6% (P = 0.039), with significantly better recurrence-free survival (log-rank P = 0.039). Combined navigation was an independent protective factor for postoperative complications (OR = 0.313, 95% CI 0.107–0.915; P = 0.034).

title: Psoas Major Volume Asymmetry, Not Attachment Site Asymmetry, is Associated with Chronic Low Back Pain Status
abstract: Abstract Purpose To determine whether psoas major muscle (PMM) volume and attachment-site asymmetry are associated with chronic low back pain (CLBP). Exploratory analyses examined associations between PMM volume asymmetry and disability, physical activity, and age. Methods This retrospective secondary analysis included adults aged 35–65 years with and without CLBP from the NIH-sponsored BACPAC imaging cohort. Participants were propensity score matched on age, BMI, and sex. Automated segmentation (MuscleMap) was used to quantify bilateral PMM volumes, and volume asymmetry was calculated as the percent difference between left and right volumes. Attachment-site asymmetry was assessed using axial and coronal MRI classifications. Binary logistic regression evaluated associations between PMM volume and attachment-site asymmetry and CLBP status. Exploratory multiple linear regression evaluated associations between PMM volume asymmetry and disability, physical activity, age, and CLBP status. Results Greater PMM volume asymmetry was associated with higher odds of CLBP (OR = 1.08 per 1% increase, 95% CI 1.02–1.14, p = .007). Neither axial nor coronal attachment-site asymmetry was significantly associated with CLBP. The exploratory model was not statistically significant ( F (4,172) = 2.01, p = .095), and disability, physical activity, age, and CLBP status were not individually significantly associated with PMM volume asymmetry. Conclusion Greater PMM volume asymmetry was associated with CLBP, whereas attachment-site asymmetry was not. These findings support further investigation of PMM volume asymmetry as a morphological feature associated with CLBP.

title: Influence of body composition on survival in breast cancer patients with bone metastasis: a clinicopathologic-radiomic web-based nomogram development and validation
abstract: Abstract Background Bone metastasis (BM) reduces survival in breast cancer (BC) patients. Altered body composition is prognostic but poorly captured by conventional models; radiomics enables precise CT-based quantification. This study aimed to determine the influence of body composition on survival in BC patients with BM and to develop and validate a comprehensive web-based nomogram. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 197 breast cancer patients with bone metastasis at Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute & Hospital, Tianjin, China, between January 2010 and December 2017. Another 38 patients from January 2012 to December 2016 in P.A. Hertsen Moscow Oncology Research Center, Moscow, Russia, as the external validation cohort to test the nomogram. The radiomics score for predicting survival was established by using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator Cox regression. The Kaplan-Meier method was used for survival analysis. Multivariable Cox regression analysis was used to construct a clinicopathologic-radiomic web-based nomogram based on clinicopathologic and radiomics features of body composition. A clinicopathologic web-based nomogram was also established. Receiver operating characteristic curves and internal validation cohort were used to evaluate aforementioned nomograms. We verified the clinicopathologic-radiomic web-based nomogram model using the external validation cohort. Results The Kaplan-Meier analysis showed the 1-year survival in breast cancer patients with bone metastasis in construction cohort was 81.9%, the 3-year was 48.6%, the 5-year was 19.6%. Body composition was proved to be significantly correlated with the prognosis of breast cancer patients with bone metastasis. Eight variables were selected into the clinicopathologic-radiomic model: radscore, bone CT-value, bone metastasis location, pathology subtype, brain metastasis, ALP, Ca and TMI. The clinicopathologic-radiomic web-based nomogram was satisfactory with the C-index of 0.82, which was higher than the clinicopathologic model (C-index was 0.71). The AUCs of clinicopathologic-radiomic web-based nomogram in 1-, 3-, 5-years were internally validated (82.3%, 91.1% and 82.9%, respectively) and externally validated (85.1%, 84.3% and 67.7%, respectively). Conclusions Body composition was significantly associated with the prognosis of breast cancer patients with bone metastasis. Individualized rehabilitation training and nutritional support intervention should be encouraged for the patients. The established clinicopathologic-radiomic nomogram was an effective tool for prognostic prediction, and could help clinicians make personalized clinical decisions.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Inter-Incisal Mouth Opening in Patients with Oral Submucous Fibrosis with or without Impacted 3rd Molar as a Risk Factor- An observational study
abstract: Abstract Background In rural settings, kharra chewing is highly prevalent among young individuals, leading to an increased incidence of oral submucous fibrosis (OSMF) at an early age. As impacted third molars (I3Ms) are also more common in this age group, they may further contribute to restricted mouth opening. However, evidence regarding the influence of I3Ms on inter-incisal mouth opening (IMO) in patients with OSMF is scarce. Third molar extraction has never been mentioned in the surgical or medical treatment of OSMF. Therefore, this study aimed to comparatively evaluate the IMO in OSMF patients with and without I3Ms and as a risk factor. Methods The status of I3Ms in OSMF patients with a chronic habit history of areca nut quid chewing was assessed in the age range of 18–35 years in Wardha district. A total of 100 OSMF patients who attended the dental outpatient clinic of the Department of Oral Medicine and Radiology (OMR) over a 6-month period were selected for the study. The absence or presence of I3Ms was evaluated on panoramic radiographs. The correlation between the OSMF and impacted third molars was explored using a chi-square test at a 5% level of significance (P < = 0.05). Results A total of 100 patients with OSMF (18–35 years; 84% males, 16% females) were included. Based on the Chandramani More et al. (2012) staging system, 40% were Grade II, 24% were Grade I, 22% were Grade III, and 14% were Grade IV. Impacted third molars (I3Ms) were present in 48% of patients, while retromolar fibrous bands were identified in 42%. Both I3Ms and retromolar fibrous bands were present in 27% of patients, whereas 15% had fibrous bands alone, 21% had I3Ms alone, and 37% had neither. A substantial correlation was observed between OSMF stage and the coexistence of retromolar fibrous bands with I3Ms, with the highest frequency noted in Grade II patients. Conclusions The co-existence of impacted third molars and OSMF may further restrict mouth opening, potentially leading to an overestimation or pseudo-grading of OSMF severity. This may result in inappropriate or over-treatment. Therefore, a thorough clinical and radiographic evaluation is essential to differentiate the contribution of impacted third molars from OSMF-related trismus, ensuring accurate disease grading and appropriate treatment planning. Trial registration no.: Not applicable

title: Individualized Structural Brain Deviations in Bipolar I Disorder: a Normative Modeling Study of 4 660 ENIGMA Participants
abstract: Abstract Bipolar disorder (BD) is a prevalent psychiatric condition characterized by marked clinical and neuroanatomical heterogeneity. Prior neuroimaging studies have used case-control comparisons yielding small to moderate effect sizes for group differences. Large and diverse samples are needed to map heterogeneity within BD. Here, we used individualized brain morphometry deviations derived from normative modeling for three MRI-based measures (regional cortical thickness, regional surface area, and subcortical volumes). In addition, ROI-level deviations in the left middle temporal gyrus and the left inferior temporal gyrus were associated with longer illness duration. This is the largest study to date exploring individualized deviations as neuroanatomical features associated with bipolar disorder. Our findings suggest that neuroanatomical heterogeneity is a core feature of bipolar disorder, with preferential left-lateralized cortical-hippocampal involvement pointing to spatially structured heterogeneity.

title: Type III Popliteal Artery Branching Variants: Morphometric Characterization, Preoperative CTA Assessment, and Clinical Implications for Lower-Leg Flap Surgery: A Cohort Study and Meta-Analysis
abstract: Abstract Background. This study aimed to systematically characterize the prevalence and morphometric features of Type III popliteal artery branching variants in a computed tomography angiography (CTA) cohort of Chinese patients, and to derive global prevalence estimates and identify sources of heterogeneity via meta-analysis. Methods. This retrospective cohort comprised 235 consecutive patients (470 lower extremities) who underwent bilateral lower-extremity CTA between April 2020 and December 2024. Branching patterns were classified according to the Kim-Lippert system. CTA images were reviewed for popliteal artery branching and anatomical variations. Morphometric assessment included proximal diameters at the tibiofibular neck, terminal diameters of compensatory vessels, hypoplasia/aplasia classification, termination-point localization, and target-artery-to-peroneal-artery (PA) diameter ratios. Four databases were searched for the meta-analysis. Pooled prevalence was estimated using a random-effects model with Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation. Results. Type III variants were identified in 24 patients (10.21%) and 32 limbs (6.81%), comprising Type IIIA (3.19% limbs), IIIB (2.55% limbs), IIIC (0.21% limbs), and IIID (0.85% limbs). Two atypical peri-ankle collateral-dominant patterns were observed in 5 limbs (1.06%). Target-artery reductions were pronounced, with proximal diameter reductions of 31.9–33.3% accompanied by reciprocal PA enlargement of 15.3–16.9% proximally and 23.6–25.6% terminally. The target-artery-to-PA ratio reversed from 1.25 in normal limbs to 0.73 in IIIA and 0.65 in IIIB. Across 30 studies (10,351 limbs), pooled prevalences were 90.93% for Type I, 3.30% for IIIA, 1.46% for IIIB, 0.56% for IIIC, and 0.13% for IIID, with moderate to substantial heterogeneity (I² = 46.1–87.1%). Meta-regression showed that CT-based detection was associated with lower Type IIIC prevalence, and larger sample size as predictive of lower IIID prevalence. Conclusions. Type III popliteal artery variants were relatively common in this cohort of Chinese patients. In IIIA and IIIB, tibial deficiency was accompanied by peroneal artery enlargement, whereas IIID showed peroneal deficiency with preserved tibial runoff; IIIC was too rare for morphometric inference. Recognition of these patterns on preoperative CTA, including atypical peri-ankle collateral variants, is therefore prudent to ensure safe performance of lower-extremity microsurgical and orthopedic procedures. Trial registration: Not applicable.

title: DSPAN: Dual-domain structure-aware adversarial learning with physics-inspired consistency for low-dose CT denoising
abstract: Abstract Background Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces radiation exposure but increases noise and artifacts that can obscure low-contrast anatomy. We developed the Dual-domain Structure-Preserving Adversarial Network (DSPAN) to improve LDCT image fidelity. Methods DSPAN combines a ResNet-based generator with dual-domain structure-aware attention and coupled gradient- and frequency-consistency learning. We used five-fold patient-level cross-validation on all 10 patients in the 2016 NIH-AAPM-Mayo Clinic Low Dose CT Grand Challenge dataset. Each fold included seven training patients, one validation patient for checkpoint selection, and two test patients. Every patient was tested once. Slice-level measurements were averaged within each patient, and performance was summarized descriptively across the 10 patients. No null-hypothesis tests were performed. Results DSPAN achieved a mean peak signal-to-noise ratio of 40.2105 ± 1.6183 dB, structural similarity of 0.9424 ± 0.0220, and root mean squared error of 2.5359 ± 0.5303 in 8-bit-equivalent units. It had the best mean value for all six evaluated image-quality metrics. Compared with DU-GAN, mean peak signal-to-noise ratio increased by 0.1505 dB and root mean squared error decreased by 0.0410. Module ablation showed a 1.0662 dB mean peak signal-to-noise ratio gain over ResNetGAN alone. Conclusions Combining structure-aware attention with gradient and frequency consistency improved internal image-quality performance in this 10-patient dataset. External validation and diagnostic reader studies are needed to establish generalizability and clinical relevance.

title: Deep Learning and Multi-Omics for Lung Cancer TME Risk Stratification
abstract: Abstract Objective Immune checkpoint inhibitors are increasingly used in elderly lung cancer patients, yet treatment response varies widely due to tumor immune microenvironment (TME) heterogeneity. This study aimed to develop a CT image-based deep learning model for TME risk stratification in elderly patients (≥ 60 years) and to explore the underlying imaging-transcriptomic mechanisms. Methods Transcriptomic and clinical data for 436 elderly lung cancer patients were obtained from TCGA, with matched CT images from TCIA. Tumor segmentation was performed using nnU-Net, followed by feature extraction via a 3D residual network. The DeepSurv model was constructed combining imaging features with clinical variables. Multi-omics analyses included differential expression, functional enrichment, immune microenvironment assessment (CIBERSORT/ESTIMATE/ssGSEA), WGCNA, and Lasso-Cox regression. External validation used ICGC and GEO immunotherapy datasets. Results The nnU-Net model achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.858. The DeepSurv fusion model attained a C-index of 0.748, outperforming clinical models (0.668). High-risk patients had significantly shorter median overall survival than low-risk patients (13.4 vs. 23.8 months, P < 0.001). A 12-gene signature was identified, enriched in extracellular matrix remodeling, TGF-β signaling, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. The high-risk group exhibited increased M2 macrophage and regulatory T-cell infiltration with reduced CD8⁺ T cells, indicating an immunosuppressive phenotype. The signature stratified survival in the ICGC cohort (P = 0.002). Imaging-molecular correlation confirmed that imaging features reflect key immunosuppressive mechanisms. Conclusion This CT-based deep learning model effectively identifies elderly lung cancer patients with an immunosuppressive TME, offering superior risk stratification over traditional models. The imaging-molecular correlation supports CT imaging as a potential non-invasive tool for TME assessment and immunotherapy decision-making in elderly patients.

title: Optimization of Post-processing Reconstruction for Orthopedic Metal Implants on Photon-Counting Detector CT: A Within-Patient Comparison
abstract: Abstract Objectives To determine how iterative metal artifact reduction (iMAR), virtual monoenergetic imaging (VMI), and reconstruction kernel selection affect metal artifacts and image quality around orthopedic implants on photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT), and to identify task-specific reconstructions for bone and soft-tissue evaluation. Materials and methods This retrospective within-patient study included 10 patients with 11 orthopedic implant sites. All reconstructions were generated from the same PCD-CT raw data. Three predefined comparisons were performed: iMAR off versus on at 70 keV/Br40/1.0 mm; four bone reconstructions combining T3D or 145-keV VMI with Qr64 or Br64 at 0.4 mm; and four soft-tissue reconstructions combining T3D or 65-keV VMI with Br40 or Qr40 at 1.0 mm. CT attenuation, image noise, artifact index (AI), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), 5-point Likert scores, and interreader agreement were evaluated. Results With matched parameters, iMAR increased median bone scores from 2 to 4 and soft-tissue scores from 1 to 2–3. For bone, 145-keV VMI reduced image noise and AI compared with T3D; 145-keV Br64 had the highest subjective scores, whereas 145-keV Qr64 showed the most favorable quantitative metrics. For soft tissue, T3D had lower noise and AI and higher SNR than 65-keV VMI, and T3D Br40 received the highest subjective scores. Weighted κ ranged from 0.635 to 0.717. Conclusion Post-processing optimization on PCD-CT was task specific. iMAR improved image evaluability, 145-keV VMI favored bone and bone-implant interface assessment, and T3D Br40 favored adjacent soft-tissue evaluation.

title: Early risk stratification for in-hospital mortality and 6-month unfavourable prognosis after injury in traumatic brain injury: machine learning models for clinical decision support
abstract: Abstract Purpose To develop and externally validate machine-learning models using routinely available early admission data for in-hospital death and 6-month unfavourable prognosis after injury in traumatic brain injury (TBI). Methods This retrospective multicentre prognostic study included patients aged ≥ 15 years admitted within 12 h after TBI at four Chinese hospitals from November 2020 to October 2025. Two hospitals were used for development and two for independent external testing. Predictors included age, neurological assessments, laboratory measurements, and head computed tomography (CT) findings. Laboratory measurements were standardised using Value/upper limit of normal (ULN). Models were selected internally and evaluated using discrimination, classification, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Results The in-hospital death analysis included 2260 patients (523 deaths, 23.1%); the 6-month unfavourable prognosis after injury analysis included 1512 discharge survivors with available follow-up (254 unfavourable outcomes, 16.8%). For in-hospital death, CatBoost using features selected by Lasso-Logistic regression achieved external area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) 0.903 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.883–0.922), area under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC) 0.800 (95% CI, 0.760–0.844), sensitivity 82.0%, positive predictive value (PPV) 71.1%, and F1 score 76.2%. For 6-month unfavourable prognosis after injury, logistic regression using features selected by XGBoost-based recursive feature elimination with cross-validation (RFECV-XGBoost) achieved external AUROC 0.906 (95% CI, 0.873–0.936), AUPRC 0.727 (95% CI, 0.642–0.823), sensitivity 81.1%, PPV 72.5%, and F1 score 76.6%. Conclusion Both models maintained consistent cross-centre predictive performance and may support early risk stratification and treatment planning after TBI. Prospective multicentre evaluation is still needed before implementation.

title: Partially thrombosed distal anterior cerebral artery aneurysm mimicking a brain tumor in a child
abstract: Abstract Partially thrombosed intracranial aneurysms may resemble neoplasms when only a small lumen remains patent and the thrombosed sac becomes the dominant mass. A 10-year-old boy with remote closed head trauma was found to have a progressively enlarging midline cystic-solid lesion. Computed tomography angiography and digital subtraction angiography demonstrated a partially thrombosed aneurysm arising from a terminal branch of the left A3 segment. Serial imaging showed enlargement of both the thrombosed sac and the posterior cystic component. Because occlusion of the residual lumen alone would not relieve the mass effect, we used a left anterior interhemispheric approach for vascular control and decompression. After proximal and distal control, the sac was opened, the organized thrombus was removed, and the cystic component was fenestrated. The aneurysm was then resected without reconstruction because the main pericallosal trunk remained intact. Postoperative imaging confirmed complete resection, decompression, and preserved distal anterior cerebral artery circulation. The patient had no new neurological deficit. In a child with a tumor-like midline lesion, vascular imaging should precede biopsy. The treatment plan should account for the thrombosed and cystic components as well as the patent lumen.

title: Comprehensive Treatment of a Patient with Osteogenesis Imperfecta and Congenital Hemivertebra: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is a rare hereditary connective tissue disorder characterized by extreme bone fragility, making the surgical management of associated severe scoliosis exceptionally challenging due to the high risk of instrumentation failure. The coexistence of OI and a congenital hemivertebra in a single patient is exceedingly rare and further complicates spinal deformity correction. We report the case of a 17-year-old boy with OI who presented with progressive, severe thoracolumbar scoliosis and worsening lumbar pain. Imaging revealed major Cobb angles of 85° and 95°, a fully segmented L3 hemivertebra, and markedly reduced bone mineral density with a total lumbar Z-score of –5.8. To optimize surgical safety and outcomes, a comprehensive, multidisciplinary treatment strategy was implemented. This included preoperative halo-gravity traction to improve spinal flexibility and alignment, alongside bisphosphonate therapy to enhance bone mass. The patient underwent a posterior L3 vertebrectomy and spinal fusion from T4 to S1. Postoperative radiographs demonstrated satisfactory deformity correction. Although asymptomatic pedicle screw breakage was observed at the 6-month follow-up—highlighting the immense biomechanical stress posed by the inherent bone fragility in OI—the patient maintained stable spinal alignment without significant loss of correction at 12 months. This case underscores that while meticulous perioperative optimization (including traction and pharmacological therapies) combined with advanced surgical planning can achieve successful deformity correction in patients with OI and congenital scoliosis, continuous long-term monitoring remains vital due to the persistent risk of hardware fatigue. Trial registration Not applicable. This study is a case report and not a clinical trial.

title: Development and internal validation of a CSF-free machine-learning model to distinguish immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced encephalitis from HSV-1 and anti-LGI1 encephalitis
abstract: Abstract Background Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced encephalitis (ICI-iE) is difficult to distinguish from herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) and anti-LGI1 encephalitis, and its work-up includes invasive cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) testing. We evaluated whether a model excluding CSF features could achieve discrimination similar to a CSF-inclusive model and support triage before lumbar puncture. Methods We reanalysed 51 complete cases (ICI-iE, 19; HSV-1, 20; anti-LGI1, 12) from a publicly available retrospective dataset combining registry-based ICI-iE cases with single-centre HSV-1 and anti-LGI1 comparators. Random-forest models with 29 features (including CSF) or 25 features (excluding CSF) were evaluated by repeated nested cross-validation (5 outer folds × 20 repeats). We assessed discrimination, calibration, decision curves, out-of-fold TreeSHAP values, and a hypothetical high-specificity rule-in strategy across assumed prevalences. Results Mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) across repeats were 0.894 with CSF and 0.902 without CSF. On the repeat-averaged out-of-fold predictions, AUCs were 0.911 with CSF and 0.908 without CSF, and an approximate DeLong comparison showed no significant difference (ΔAUC [with CSF minus without CSF], + 0.003; 95% CI, − 0.033 to + 0.040; p = 0.86). Encephalitis-typical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings and C-reactive protein were the leading contributors. In an exploratory sensitivity analysis, additionally excluding MRI features from the CSF-free model yielded a mean cross-validated AUC of 0.769. At specificity of 0.967–0.973, sensitivity was 0.574–0.597. Under the hypothetical rule-in strategy, the true-positive classification proportion was 21%–22% at the cohort prevalence (37.3%) but 3%–6% at 5%–10% prevalence. False-positive classification remained 2–3% of patients across the evaluated prevalence scenarios. Calibration was poor. Conclusions In this small internally validated dataset, excluding CSF features did not materially lower the point estimate of discrimination, whereas discrimination depended substantially, but not exclusively, on MRI findings. The CSF-free model may support triage while confirmatory testing is pending but should not replace CSF testing to exclude HSV-1 encephalitis. External validation in standardised, representative cohorts is required, particularly given potential confounding by data source.

Methods We reanalysed 51 complete cases (ICI-iE, 19; HSV-1, 20; anti-LGI1, 12) from a publicly available retrospective dataset combining registry-based ICI-iE cases with single-centre HSV-1 and anti-LGI1 comparators. Random-forest models with 29 features (including CSF) or 25 features (excluding CSF) were evaluated by repeated nested cross-validation (5 outer folds × 20 repeats). We assessed discrimination, calibration, decision curves, out-of-fold TreeSHAP values, and a hypothetical high-specificity rule-in strategy across assumed prevalences. Results Mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) across repeats were 0.894 with CSF and 0.902 without CSF. On the repeat-averaged out-of-fold predictions, AUCs were 0.911 with CSF and 0.908 without CSF, and an approximate DeLong comparison showed no significant difference (ΔAUC [with CSF minus without CSF], + 0.003; 95% CI, − 0.033 to + 0.040; p = 0.86). In an exploratory sensitivity analysis, additionally excluding MRI features from the CSF-free model yielded a mean cross-validated AUC of 0.769. At specificity of 0.967–0.973, sensitivity was 0.574–0.597. Under the hypothetical rule-in strategy, the true-positive classification proportion was 21%–22% at the cohort prevalence (37.3%) but 3%–6% at 5%–10% prevalence. False-positive classification remained 2–3% of patients across the evaluated prevalence scenarios. Calibration was poor. Conclusions In this small internally validated dataset, excluding CSF features did not materially lower the point estimate of discrimination, whereas discrimination depended substantially, but not exclusively, on MRI findings. External validation in standardised, representative cohorts is required, particularly given potential confounding by data source.

title: Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich Syndrome Complicated by Right Ectopic Atrophic Kidney: A Case Report from a Primary Hospital
abstract: Abstract Background Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome (HWWS), also termed obstructed hemivagina and ipsilateral renal anomaly (OHVIRA), is a rare congenital Müllerian duct anomaly frequently accompanied by structural abnormalities of the ipsilateral kidney and ureter. Owing to its nonspecific clinical features, which often overlap with common acute abdominal conditions such as pelvic inflammatory disease and appendicitis-HWWS is frequently misdiagnosed or missed in primary healthcare settings, particularly among post-menarchal adolescents with atypical symptoms. This case report presents a 9-year-old girl with HWWS and ipsilateral ectopic atrophic kidney associated with an ectopic ureteral orifice, and discusses the diagnostic reasoning, stepwise imaging strategy, and multidisciplinary management experience gained at a primary hospital. Case presentation: A 9-year-old girl presented with intermittent lower abdominal distending pain for 15 days. Menarche had occurred four months earlier; menses were irregular, without cyclic dysmenorrhea or vaginal purulent discharge. Initial pelvic ultrasonography demonstrated a mixed echogenic pelvic mass and absent right kidney. Subsequent contrast-enhanced pelvic MRI and CT urography (CTU) confirmed the diagnosis of type I HWWS, characterized by uterus didelphys with double cervix, right vaginal atresia with hematometra and hematocolpos, and a right ectopic atrophic kidney with an ectopic ureteral orifice. After multidisciplinary consultation involving gynecology, urology, and general surgery, the patient underwent combined hysteroscopic resection of the right vaginal oblique septum, laparoscopic resection of the ectopic right kidney and ureter, and cystoscopy. The intraoperative course was uneventful. Postoperative anti-infective therapy and vaginal care were provided; the patient recovered satisfactorily and was discharged on postoperative day 10 without abnormal vaginal discharge. Conclusion HWWS exhibits heterogeneous and often atypical manifestations in adolescent girls. Primary-care physicians should maintain a high index of suspicion and adopt an integrated genitourinary diagnostic mindset. A stepwise imaging strategy combining ultrasonography, MRI, and CTU can significantly improve early recognition. Combined minimally invasive surgery under multidisciplinary collaboration is safe and feasible, and may serve as a useful reference for the management of complex congenital genitourinary malformations in primary hospitals.

title: Beyond Cobb angles: The role of Coxofemoral axis based positional parameters in Sagittal Spine alignment
abstract: Abstract Background Conventional sagittal alignment assessment is largely based on angular morphological parameters and sagittal vertical axis (SVA). However, individuals with similar Cobb angles may demonstrate different sagittal profiles depending on the location of the apices of the thoracic and lumbar curves. Coxofemoral-axis-based positional parameters may therefore provide complementary information regarding global sagittal balance. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the relationships between conventional morphological parameters, global sagittal parameters, and coxofemoral-axis-based positional parameters in a healthy adults, and to identify positional measurements that may be useful in characterizing the sagittal alignment Methods This study is a Cross sectional Observational study. Standing whole-spine radiographs of 75 healthy individuals were evaluated. Morphological parameters included cervical lordosis, T1 slope, thoracic kyphosis, lumbar lordosis, sacral slope, pelvic tilt, and pelvic incidence. Positional and global sagittal parameters included SVA, thoracic apex-femoral axis distance (TF), lumbar apex-femoral axis distance (LF), S1F, overhang, thoracolumbar width (TL width), T1 pelvic angle (T1PA), T4 pelvic angle (T4PA), L1 pelvic angle (L1PA), and T1 sacropelvic inclination (T1SPI). Correlation, partial correlation, and linear regression analyses were performed to assess relationships among parameters. Results Strong correlations were observed between S1F and LF (r = 0.91), pelvic tilt and S1F (r = 0.75), overhang and S1F (r = 0.74), TF and TL width (r = 0.71), and T1SPI with both TF and TL width (r = 0.77). SVA demonstrated a strong inverse correlation with TL width (r=-0.76). Linear regression demonstrated significant relationships between S1F and LF/PT (R 2 = 0.878), overhang and PT/LF (R 2 = 0.868), SVA and TL width (R 2 = 0.684), and T1SPI with TF/TL width (approximately R 2 = 0.69; p < 0.01). Among the positional parameters, S1F demonstrated the strongest overall associations with established spinopelvic parameters, while TL width showed a particularly strong relationship with SVA. Conclusion Sagittal spine alignment is influenced by both spinal morphology and the spatial position of spinal curves. Coxofemoral-axis-based measurements provide complementary information regarding the spatial configuration of the sagittal profile. S1F appears to be a particularly useful positional descriptor of spinopelvic relationships, while TL width may serve as a simple marker of global sagittal alignment because of its strong association with SVA. Larger pathological cohorts are required to determine their clinical and prognostic relevance.

title: Mechanism-Driven Radiogenomic Analysis Reveals Potential Molecular Drivers of Pretreatment MRI Phenotypes in Breast Cancer
abstract: Abstract Purpose To develop a pretreatment MRI model for predicting residual cancer burden (RCB) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy and a mechanism-driven radiogenomic framework to identify molecular programs underlying response-associated MRI phenotypes. Methods A multimodal deep learning model was developed using pretreatment MRI and clinical data from 492 patients across two centers. Radiomic phenotypes from 61 patients were integrated with public transcriptomic cohorts using differential expression, pathway enrichment, WGCNA, survival modeling, feature selection, and in silico perturbation analyses. Results The model achieved AUCs of 0.919 in training and 0.852 in testing. Of 195 response-associated differentially expressed genes, 109 showed concordant changes in an independent cohort. Response was linked to proliferation, DNA repair, hypoxia, immune-inflammatory, and estrogen-response programs. A 12-gene prognostic signature achieved a C-index of 0.798. Multilayer prioritization identified ESR1, TBC1D9, GREB1 , and related genes, while RARRES1 uniquely showed strong directional concordance between predicted and observed radiomic changes. Conclusion Pretreatment MRI heterogeneity reflects coordinated biological programs relevant to neoadjuvant treatment response. This framework supports noninvasive RCB stratification and generates testable mechanistic hypotheses for functional validation.

title: MelanoFusion: An Explainable and Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid CNN–Transformer Framework for Dermoscopic Melanoma Detection
abstract: Abstract Melanoma is an aggressive skin cancer requiring early detection, yet automated analysis remains affected by lesion variation, calibration errors, uncertainty, and subgroup disparities. This study presents MelanoFusion, a hybrid framework integrating explainability, uncertainty estimation, and fairness-oriented representation learning for melanoma detection. It combines EfficientNetV2-S and Swin Transformer encoders with cross-attention, lesion attention, feature-pyramid processing, multi-scale transformer layers, and an uncertainty head. Images were resized to 224 × 224 and processed using hair removal, median filtering, contrast enhancement, colour normalization, and watershed-based lesion priors; U-Net was used for lesion segmentation. MelanoFusion was evaluated against DenseNet121, ResNet101, EfficientNetV2-S, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and Swin Transformer on HAM10000, ISIC 2018, and PH². Segmentation Dice was 0.878 on HAM10000 and 0.830 on PH². MelanoFusion achieved ROC-AUC values of 0.687, 0.740, and 0.844 on HAM10000, ISIC 2018, and PH², respectively. Calibration was favourable on HAM10000, with an expected calibration error of 0.116. Uncertainty was significantly associated with classification error, while subgroup analysis showed significant sensitivity differences across age groups but not sex. Ablation results indicated that several proposed components did not improve discrimination. The findings support joint evaluation of discrimination, calibration, uncertainty, explainability, and subgroup behaviour, while indicating the need for external validation and clinical evaluation before deployment.

title: Comparative Outcomes of 3D-Printed Porous Artificial Vertebral Bodies and Titanium Mesh Cages After Single-Level Anterior Cervical Corpectomy and Fusion for Cervical Spinal Stenosis With Hyperextension Injury: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Objective To compare the perioperative, clinical, and radiographic outcomes of 3D-printed porous artificial vertebral bodies and titanium mesh cages (TMCs) for anterior column reconstruction after single-level anterior cervical corpectomy and fusion (ACCF) in patients with cervical spinal stenosis combined with hyperextension injury, and to identify factors associated with postoperative subsidence. Methods This single-center retrospective comparative cohort study included 140 consecutive patients who underwent single-level ACCF between 2023 and 2025, with 70 patients in the 3D group and 70 in the TMC group. Baseline characteristics, perioperative parameters, clinical outcomes, radiographic outcomes, and complications were compared between groups. The main radiographic outcomes included subsidence, reconstructed segmental height loss (ΔH), absolute change in the C2–7 sagittal vertical axis (ΔcSVA), loss of the C2–C7 Cobb angle, and fusion rates at 6 and 12 months. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with subsidence. Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was additionally performed as a sensitivity analysis to address measured treatment-selection imbalance. Results The 3D group had a shorter operative time, less intraoperative blood loss, and a shorter hospital stay than the TMC group (all P ≤ 0.002). The JOA recovery rate was higher in the 3D group (78.0 ± 13.8% vs 69.0 ± 14.3%, P < 0.001), whereas postoperative NDI was borderline different (P = 0.050) and VAS reduction was similar between groups (P = 0.544). The 3D group showed a lower subsidence rate than the TMC group (17.1% vs 61.4%, P < 0.001), less height loss (1.0 ± 0.6 vs 2.5 ± 0.9 mm, P < 0.001), a smaller absolute change in cSVA (11.6 ± 3.1 vs 22.0 ± 5.4 mm, P < 0.001), and less loss of the C2–C7 Cobb angle (1.0 ± 0.3° vs 3.1 ± 1.4°, P < 0.001). The 6-month fusion rate was higher in the 3D group (85.7% vs 40.0%, P < 0.001), whereas the 12-month fusion rates were similar (94.3% vs 88.6%, P = 0.366). Multivariable analysis showed that use of a 3D-printed vertebral body was associated with lower odds of subsidence (adjusted OR 0.035, 95% CI 0.010–0.116, P < 0.001). Each 10-HU decrease in the lower adjacent vertebral body (OR 1.189, 95% CI 1.096–1.291, P < 0.001) and each 1-mm increase in immediate postoperative reconstructed height (OR 1.417, 95% CI 1.090–1.840, P = 0.009) were associated with higher odds of subsidence. The IPTW sensitivity analysis yielded a directionally consistent association (OR 0.078, 95% CI 0.032–0.185, P < 0.001). Conclusions In patients with cervical spinal stenosis combined with hyperextension injury undergoing single-level ACCF, use of a 3D-printed porous artificial vertebral body was associated with lower postoperative subsidence, less radiographic change, and a higher early fusion rate than TMC reconstruction. The difference in fusion was no longer significant at 12 months, suggesting a potential benefit mainly in accelerating early fusion rather than increasing the ultimate likelihood of fusion. Lower adjacent vertebral HU values and greater immediate postoperative reconstructed height were also associated with higher odds of subsidence. Because of the retrospective nonrandomized design, these findings require further validation in prospective multicenter studies.

title: The Importance of Liver Density on CT Scan in Heart Failure Patients
abstract: Abstract Introduction Heart failure (HF) is a major global health problem associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Hepatic involvement is common in HF and may reflect the severity of systemic congestion and impaired hemodynamics. Although liver function tests and bilirubin levels have been investigated as prognostic markers in HF, the clinical significance of liver density measured by computed tomography (CT) has received less attention. This study aimed to evaluate the association between liver density on CT scans and clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic, and prognostic parameters in patients with HF. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 145 patients with HF admitted to a tertiary heart center between 2020 and 2022. Adults with HF with reduced or mid-range ejection fraction confirmed by echocardiography were included. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, chest CT, and echocardiographic data were obtained from medical records. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 24.0. Continuous variables were expressed as mean ± standard deviation and categorical variables as frequencies. Associations were assessed using independent t-tests and chi-square tests. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results The mean age was 42.8 ± 10.5 years, and the mean BMI was 27.06 ± 4.44 kg/m². Most patients were male. Edema and ascites were positively associated with liver density, whereas LVEDD (r = − 0.32) and SPAP (r = − 0.276) showed significant negative correlations. No significant association was observed between liver density and TAPSE (r = 0.056). Electrolytes, creatinine, and liver function tests were also associated with liver density. Patients with cardiac-related mortality had a mean liver density of 47.29 ± 7.1 HU, and this association was statistically significant (P = 0.029). Conclusion Liver density measured on chest CT may provide useful prognostic information in patients with HF and could serve as an additional imaging marker for clinical risk assessment.

title: CINet: Communication-aware Inter-modality Network for Distributed Multi-Modal MRI Reconstruction
abstract: Abstract AI-enabled medical imaging is increasingly moving toward distributed acquisition, computing, and inference, where information required by a downstream task may reside at different nodes. In multi-modal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction, this situation arises when a fully sampled auxiliary contrast is not locally available but can provide complementary information for reconstructing an undersampled target contrast. Existing methods generally assume direct access to the auxiliary modality and therefore do not consider the communication constraints involved in transferring such information between distributed nodes. To address this problem, we propose the Communication-aware Inter-modality Network (CINet) for distributed multi-modal MRI reconstruction, which jointly considers auxiliary representation transmission and cross-modal reconstruction under communication constraints. Specifically, a Task-Oriented Communication Encoder reweights multi-scale auxiliary features and generates compact representations under a prescribed communication budget. The resulting representations are transmitted through a noisy channel, and a Target-Conditioned Selective Fusion module selectively incorporates the received auxiliary information according to the current target representation. CINet thus coordinates compact auxiliary information transmission with its downstream utilization for target reconstruction. Experiments on multi-modal prostate MRI demonstrate that CINet achieves competitive or superior reconstruction performance under different undersampling patterns and acceleration factors while preserving local structural details. Further evaluations under varying communication budgets and channel signal-to-noise ratios characterize the communication--reconstruction trade-off under different transmission conditions.
