title: Effect of Natural Standing and Rest on Solute Transport Pathways in Hypermobile and Immobile Human Lumbar Intervertebral Discs. Results from Delayed Post-Contrast Upright MRI Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose To examine how physiological states of resting and standing effect the nutrient transport in mobile, hypermobile and immobile lumbar intervertebral discs. Methods This prospective study included 15 healthy participants (10 males, 5 females; mean age, 25.2 ± 3.6 years), divided into three groups: normally mobile, hypermobile (bilateral L5 pars defects), and immobile (lumbosacral transitional vertebrae), with five participants per group. Six-hour delayed post-contrast (0.3mmol/kg) T1-weighted MR images were obtained using a 0.25-T upright positional MRI system in supine, standing, and immediate post-standing recovery positions. Three-dimensional segmentation using 3D Slicer enabled regional enhancement analysis of the central nucleus pulposus (CNP), peripheral nucleus pulposus (PNP), and superior and inferior endplate zones. Results Normal discs showed standing-associated enhancement loss (wash-out) in both CNP and PNP, followed by recovery, particularly peripherally. Hypermobile discs demonstrated the largest standing-associated reduction in CNP enhancement of approximately 2.8 times that of normal discs, with incomplete regain in recovery position. Immobile discs demonstrated the greatest peripheral enhancement loss and limited central recovery. Their superior endplate exhibited a marked, reversible enhancement increase during standing, while the inferior endplate showed comparatively little positional variation. Conclusions For the first time, present study documented acute effects of natural standing and rest on solute transport of human lumbar discs with different mobility patterns in vivo. Despite similar morphology, discs at hypermobile and immobile segments demonstrated different patterns of enhancement wash-out on standing as well as different recovery patterns during rest.

title: PG-HSAM: Prototype-Guided Hierarchical Segment Anything Model for Medical Image Segmentation with Limited Annotations
abstract: Abstract Adapting segmentation foundation models to medical images with limited annotations requires effective use of semantic information without substantially increasing model complexity. We propose PG-HSAM, an extension of H-SAM that introduces prototype prior fusion (PPF) and balanced pixel-to-prototype contrastive regularization (BPC). PPF maintains exponential-moving-average class prototypes, converts pixel-to-prototype similarities into a semantic probability prior, and fuses this prior with the first-stage prediction before hierarchical refinement. BPC regularizes the same feature space with class-balanced pixel sampling. For binary segmentation, foreground and background prototypes are jointly normalized to construct the semantic prior. The prototype memory is non-trainable, and BPC is used only during training. Under the limited-label protocols of H-SAM, PG-HSAM achieves mean Dice scores of 80.49%, 85.20%, and 83.51% on Synapse, LA, and PROMISE12, respectively. Compared with H-SAM, the gains are 0.81, 1.26, and 6.56 percentage points, while Synapse HD95 decreases from 18.35 to 13.70. Ablation and hyperparameter studies further verify the contributions of PPF and BPC and show that the improvement is obtained without increasing the model parameter count.

title: Incremental Value of Pretreatment 18F-FAPI PET/CT and MRI for Predicting Early Treatment Response and Long-Term Prognosis in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Undergoing Chemoradiotherapy​
abstract: Abstract Objectives Effective noninvasive tools for predicting treatment response and prognosis in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) remain lacking. This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of integrating pretreatment 18 F-fibroblast activation protein inhibitor positron emission tomography/computed tomography ( 18 F-FAPI PET/CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for short-term complete response (CR) and progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with NPC undergoing chemoradiotherapy. Materials and Methods This retrospective study analyzed pretreatment 18 F-FAPI PET/CT and contrast-enhanced MRI (CE-MRI) parameters in 46 patients with NPC who underwent chemoradiotherapy. Logistic regression identified predictors of CR and developed predictive models, which were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, DeLong test, bootstrap internal validation, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Cox regression identified independent predictors of PFS, while Kaplan–Meier analysis and log-rank test evaluated survival outcomes. Results Nineteen patients (41.3%) achieved CR, whereas 27 (58.7%) did not. Total lesion fibroblast activation protein expression (TLF), signal intensity ratio (SIR), and radiologic extranodal extension (rENE) independently predicted CR. A multimodal model incorporating these variables achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.88, outperforming PET/CT-only (AUC = 0.76) and MRI-only (AUC = 0.79) models numerically. A maximum standardized uptake value of the primary lesion (SUVmax-T) ≥ 17.0 and the presence of rENE independently predicted shorter PFS. The Sankey diagram illustrated that high-risk parameter combinations were associated with non-CR and shorter PFS, while short-term CR was strongly concordant with longer PFS. Conclusion Pretreatment 18 F-FAPI PET/CT and MRI provide complementary information that may improve short-term response assessment and prognostic stratification in NPC.

title: Saccadic network dysfunction underlies eye-movement variability in early Parkinson's disease
abstract: Abstract Parkinson’s disease is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by altered subcortical-cortical connectivity, leading to motor and cognitive deficits. Saccadic eye movement abnormalities are among the earliest and most persistent markers of the disease, serving as sensitive indicators of disrupted oculomotor and cognitive control. While changes in average saccadic behavioral measures are widely reported in Parkinson's disease, intra-individual variability in saccadic performance and the underlying network dysfunction remain poorly understood. Here, we quantified intra-individual saccadic variability in early-stage Parkinson’s disease and identified its functional correlates within the resting-state saccadic network. We analyzed data from the inclusion visit of 91 patients with early-stage Parkinson’s disease and 46 healthy controls from the ICEBERG cohort (monocentric prospective research study) who underwent oculomotor testing and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging. First, at the behavioral level, we assessed intra-individual variability in saccadic performance within each group using the coefficient of variation of reaction time and normalized peak velocity across trials. Second, at the brain level, we assessed group differences in static and dynamic functional connectivity across 39 regions comprising the saccadic network. We examined the relationship between network connectivity and saccadic variability using partial least squares analysis. We also quantified network organization using graph-theory measures of global efficiency and clustering coefficient. Finally, we tested the relevance of intra-individual saccadic variability and network features in distinguishing patients from healthy controls using a multivariate Mahalanobis classifier. Our results showed that, compared to HC, patients had higher intra-individual variability in saccadic behavioral measures of reaction time (p Holm = 0.012) and normalized peak velocity (p Holm = 0.012). Interestingly, patients had (i) reduced static and dynamic connectivity within the saccadic network and (ii) weaker associations between network connectivity and intra-individual saccadic variability of specifically normalized peak velocity. These results were particularly driven by regions within the cognitive saccade network. The classifier that integrated intra-individual saccadic variability and network connectivity achieved 95.62% accuracy in distinguishing patients from healthy controls, with dynamic connectivity contributing more strongly to classification performance than static connectivity. We demonstrate that elevated intra-individual variability of saccades, underpinned by altered functional connectivity within cognitive-oculomotor networks, is a prominent feature of early-stage Parkinson’s disease. Emerging as a promising physiological marker of disease pathophysiology, intra-individual variability offers a powerful new framework to refine early diagnosis and improve the tracking of neurodegeneration before severe clinical milestones are reached.

title: Epicardial adipose tissue volume and the Naples Prognostic Score add incremental value to EuroSCORE II for predicting MACE after TAVR: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a common degenerative valvular disease in the elderly, and transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is now its mainstream treatment. Conventional risk scores based on demographic and comorbidity data do not capture local cardiac inflammation or systemic nutritional status, limiting prediction of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) after TAVR. Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) volume and the Naples Prognostic Score (NPS) reflect these dimensions, but their combined incremental value is unknown. We assessed their independent and incremental value for MACE after TAVR, using EuroSCORE II as reference. Methods In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 427 consecutive patients with severe CAVD undergoing TAVR (January 2020 to July 2025) were enrolled. EAT volume was quantified on computed tomography angiography and dichotomized at the cohort median; NPS was derived from routine laboratory indices and categorized as low (0–2) or high (3–4). The endpoint was MACE after TAVR, defined by Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria. Multivariable Cox regression assessed independent prognostic value; nested models were compared by Harrell’s C-index, time-dependent ROC, net reclassification index (NRI), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) and decision curve analysis. Proportional hazards were assessed. Results During a median follow-up of 24.51 months, 89 patients (20.8%) experienced MACE. After adjustment, both high EAT and high NPS were independent predictors, with average hazard ratios (HRs) of 3.01 (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.80–5.03; P < 0.001) and 1.96 (95% CI 1.27–3.04; P = 0.003). Adding both markers raised the C-index from 0.716 to 0.751 (likelihood-ratio P < 0.001); the 24-month area under the curve was 0.757. Integrated discrimination improvement was 0.068 (95% CI 0.031–0.134; P = 0.011) and net reclassification index was 0.075 (95% CI − 0.081–0.239; P = 0.345). Calibration and sensitivity analyses supported the model; time-varying analysis showed that the effect of high EAT increased over follow-up whereas that of high NPS was confined to the early period. Conclusions Preoperative EAT volume and NPS are independent, complementary predictors of MACE after TAVR. Their combination improves on conventional risk scores and requires only routine preoperative examinations.

Integrated discrimination improvement was 0.068 (95% CI 0.031–0.134; P  = 0.011) and net reclassification index was 0.075 (95% CI − 0.081–0.239; P  = 0.345). Calibration and sensitivity analyses supported the model; time-varying analysis showed that the effect of high EAT increased over follow-up whereas that of high NPS was confined to the early period. Conclusions Preoperative EAT volume and NPS are independent, complementary predictors of MACE after TAVR. Their combination improves on conventional risk scores and requires only routine preoperative examinations.

title: Stone Volume Outperforms Linear Measurements in Predicting Ureteroscopic Laser Energy, Especially for Complex Stones
abstract: Abstract Current guidelines use linear measurements to quantify stone burden for urolithiasis, but 3D volumetric assessment may offer superior accuracy. This study compared cumulative stone length and volume as predictors of total laser energy expenditure, a surrogate for operative effort, and established volume-based energy tiers. This was a retrospective analysis of 241 ureteroscopic laser lithotripsy cases (6/10–12/31/24); cumulative stone length and volume were measured from preoperative computed tomography (CT) imaging. Log-transformed multivariable regression predicted laser energy (Joules), controlling for stone number, staghorn status, and Hounsfield units (HU). Regression tree analysis identified distinct energy tiers. Volume predicted laser energy near proportionally (β = 0.93), whereas length overestimated it (β = 1.60). Volume's predictive advantage grew with complexity: for > 3 stones, length lost nearly all predictive value (R 2 = 0.02) while volume remained stable (R 2 = 0.30). For stones ≥ 20 mm, volume doubled length's performance (R 2 = 0.50 vs. 0.22; 36% narrower residual IQR). For volumes ≥ 500 mm³, volume tripled length's performance (R 2 = 0.40 vs. 0.12; 31% narrower residual IQR). Predictive performance was equivalent in low-complexity cases. Regression tree modeling established four energy tiers: <1,235 mm 3 with HU < 1,080 (2,477 J); <1,235 mm 3 with HU ≥ 1,080 (4,940 J); 1,235-2,505 mm 3 (9,625 J); and ≥ 2,505 mm 3 (21,940 J). Laser energy expenditure correlates better with stone volume than length, particularly in complex cases (multiple, large, or dense stones). Stone volumes > 1235 mm 3 and density > 1080 HU emerged as clinically important thresholds for greater laser energy requirement.

title: Predicting Outcomes in Neonatal Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy Treated with Therapeutic Hypothermia: Prognostic Values of Selected Real-World Markers from a Single- Centre Study
abstract: Abstract Background To verify the accuracy and reliability of clinically applicable prognostic markers assessed by neonatologists—specifically, background amplitude-integrated electroencephalography (aEEG) at 24 and 36 hours and the presence of abnormal posterior limb of the internal capsule (PLIC) signaling on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)—for predicting mortality and long-term morbidity in newborns undergoing therapeutic hypothermia. Methods This retrospective cohort study included newborns admitted to a tertiary perinatal center (2009–2020) for therapeutic hypothermia. Background aEEG recordings at 24 and 36 hours of life and the presence of abnormal PLIC imaging were evaluated. The ability of these markers to predict mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes was statistically tested. Results Of the 80 infants with complete follow-up data, 15 (18.75%) died, and 17 (21.25%) had an abnormal long-term neurodevelopmental outcome. The predictive ability was as follows: aEEG at 24 hours yielded a sensitivity of 0.81 and specificity of 0.90; aEEG at 36 hours yielded a sensitivity of 0.78 and specificity of 0.83; abnormal PLIC signaling yielded a sensitivity of 0.72 and specificity of 0.77. Conclusions The tested markers demonstrate good prognostic value and are readily applicable in routine clinical practice for multimodal prognostication without requiring highly specialized radiological or neurophysiological expertise.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Paravertebral Block Combined with Local Infiltration Anesthesia Versus Local Infiltration Alone in Percutaneous Vertebroplasty for Osteoporotic Vertebral Compression Fractures: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract This retrospective cohort study evaluated the perioperative outcomes of ultrasound-guided paravertebral nerve block (PVB) combined with local infiltration anesthesia versus local infiltration alone in 84 patients undergoing percutaneous vertebroplasty (PVP) for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures. Patients were allocated to the PVB group (n = 42) or control group (n = 42). The PVB group demonstrated significantly lower intraoperative mean arterial pressure (116.2 ± 10.9 vs 131.9 ± 14.7 mmHg, P < 0.001, Cohen’s d = 1.21) and heart rate (80.9 ± 8.6 vs 87.4 ± 6.4 bpm, P = 0.0002). Postoperative Visual Analogue Scale scores were significantly lower in the PVB group at 0, 6, and 12 hours (all P ≤ 0.001) but not at 24 hours (1.26 ± 0.80 vs 1.29 ± 0.64, P = 0.697). The PVB group had shorter operative time (31.4 ± 11.1 vs 41.1 ± 6.1 min, P < 0.001) and hospital stay (median 5 vs 8 days, P = 0.001). Bone cement leakage occurred in 9.5% versus 14.3% of patients (P = 0.736). In conclusion, ultrasound-guided PVB may provide better intraoperative hemodynamic stability and reduce early postoperative pain within 12 hours, though analgesic benefits appear time-limited. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the retrospective design.

title: Exploratory Proteomics and Radiomics Correlates of [68Ga]Ga-ABY-025 PET Uptake in HER2-Low Metastatic Breast Cancer: A Pilot Study
abstract: Abstract Background Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-low metastatic breast cancer is now an actionable subtype, yet patient selection remains challenging. The aim of this work was to investigate whether multi-omics profiling (proteomics and radiomics) of paired tumor biopsies could explain the observed discordance between PET uptake, IHC score and total HER2 abundance. Methods Ten patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer underwent [ 68 Ga]Ga-ABY-025 PET/CT and tumor biopsy in a pilot clinical trial. Discovery proteomics quantified 5,341 proteins in eight patients, and CT radiomics extracted 2,046 features from nine patients (seven with both). Multi-Omics Factor Analysis (MOFA), Spearman correlations, and Enrichr pathway/transcription-factor enrichment were performed. Results Total ERBB2 (HER2) protein abundance did not correlate with SUVmax (Spearman r s = 0.19, P = 0.65). MOFA suggested a separation of the radiomics-linked latent factor (LF1) associated with HER2 (ERBB2) abundance from a proteomics-linked factor (LF3) associated with SUVmax. Top SUVmax-correlated proteins included AGPS (membrane composition), ARHGDIA (cytoskeletal remodeling) and ATAD1 (membrane protein quality control) (Spearman r ≥ 0.95). Enrichment of positive correlates implicated vesicle-mediated transport (adjusted P = 0.0024), endocytic recycling (adjusted P = 0.0087), peroxisomal function (adjusted P = 0.0015) and focal adhesion (adjusted P = 0.0007). Specific radiomics features, such as wavelet-HLL_firstorder_Minimum, correlated well with HER2 levels (r s > 0.95) ; however, none remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons in this small cohort. Conclusion In this hypothesis-generating analysis, PET uptake aligned with membrane-microenvironment proteins, rather than with total HER2 abundance. These findings are consistent with a model in which [ 68 Ga]Ga-ABY-025 uptake reflects cell-surface HER2 availability influenced by membrane trafficking, cytoskeletal organization, and endocytic recycling, and identify candidate biomarkers and radiomic signatures for validation in larger cohorts. Trial registration Clinicaltrials.gov, NCT05619016, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05619016. Date of registration Nov 30 th 2022.

title: Evaluation of a novel diagnostic kit for detecting metastatic sentinel lymph nodes in breast cancer patients using the semi-dry dot blot method combined with an automatic reader: A single-center prospective study
abstract: Abstract Background: A semi-dry dot blot (SDB) detects lymph node (LN) metastases by measuring cytokeratin (CK) in LN lavage fluid using an anti-CK antibody. We evaluated a SDB kit that combines an anti-CK19 antibody with an automatic reader for the intraoperative diagnosis of LN metastasis in patients with breast cancer. This exploratory study evaluated the diagnostic performance and identified the optimal cut-off values for detection. Methods: We analyzed 226 LNs dissected from 108 breast cancer patients who underwent sentinel LN (SLN) biopsy at Nagasaki University Hospital between January and December 2020. The SDB kit assayed proteins extracted from SLNs and an automatic reader measured CK19 absorbance. The results were compared with those of hematoxylin and eosin staining and CK19 immunohistochemistry, interpreted independently and blindly by pathologists. Cut-off values for CK19 absorbance were determined post-hoc using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Results: Among the 226 SLNs, histopathology identified 14 macrometastases (6.2%), 7 micrometastases (3.1%), and 205 metastasis-negative nodes, including one with isolated tumor cells (90.7%). Using a cut-off CK19 absorbance of 9.9 milli-absorbance units (mABS), sensitivity, specificity, and overall agreement of the SDB kit were 85.7%, 80.5%, and 81.0%, respectively. With a cut-off of 60.0 mABS to distinguish macrometastases from non-macrometastases, these values were 92.9%, 100%, and 99.6%, respectively. The assay required approximately 20 min, costing <$30 USD per test. Conclusions: This SDB kit combined with an automatic reader provided results quickly and accurately, with potentially lower implementation costs than pathologist-only diagnoses of metastases without LN tissue loss, permitting concurrent histopathology.

title: Somatostatin receptor-targeted DOTATATE PET/CT in breast cancer and breast lesions: a systematic review of detection, incidental findings and theranostic potential
abstract: Abstract Background Somatostatin receptor 2 (SSTR2) is expressed by a subset of breast cancers, particularly oestrogen receptor (ER)-positive tumours. DOTATATE PET/CT, the reference standard for neuroendocrine tumour (NET) imaging, is increasingly relevant to breast cancer staging, incidental findings and theranostic selection. We systematically reviewed its clinical performance. Methods Following PRISMA 2020 (PROSPERO CRD420261508548), Embase, Scopus and PubMed were searched to 16 September 2026, supplemented by citation searching. Studies reporting DOTATATE PET findings in breast cancer or breast lesions were included. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2 and Joanna Briggs Institute tools, certainty with GRADE, and findings were synthesised narratively. Results Nineteen studies (four prospective, two retrospective cohorts, three case series, ten case reports) including 107 patients with breast carcinoma were analysed. In head-to-head comparisons (n = 56), DOTATATE detected disease in most patients and matched 18 F-FDG for skeletal (252 vs 255 lesions) and nodal metastases, but identified half as many visceral metastases (134 vs 262), particularly in the liver. Uptake favoured ER-positive, lobular and neuroendocrine tumours. Focal breast uptake occurred on 1.1% of scans performed for other indications; 21.4% of characterised lesions were malignant and SUVmax did not discriminate benign from malignant lesions. Krenning scores ≥ 3 were found in 15/76 (19.7%) patients across three prospective studies. Certainty of evidence was very low. Conclusions DOTATATE PET/CT complements, but cannot replace, 18 F-FDG for breast cancer staging, and is less established than 18 F-FES. Incidental breast uptake warrants standard breast work-up regardless of intensity. Around one-fifth of patients with ER-positive metastatic disease show high SSTR expression, although whether this has therapeutic relevance remains uncertain.

title: Development and Multicenter Validation of a Contrast-Enhanced CT-Based Radiomics Model for Predicting Extrahepatic Metastasis after TACE in Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Objective To develop and validate a prediction model integrating pretreatment contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) radiomics with clinical features, and to evaluate its value in predicting extrahepatic metastasis (EHM) after transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) in patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods Clinical data of 152 patients with unresectable HCC who underwent TACE at the participating centers between January 2015 and December 2024 were retrospectively collected, and the patients were randomly assigned to a training set and an internal test set at a ratio of 7:3. Seventy additional HCC patients treated at other participating centers served as the external test set.Lesions were delineated on multiphase CECT images for radiomic feature extraction; after LASSO-based feature selection, the selected features were combined with independent clinical risk factors to construct prediction models and a nomogram. Model discrimination and calibration were assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), and calibration curves. The predictive performance of the models was validated using data from the external cohort. Results Multivariate analysis showed that age, alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), and maximum tumor diameter were independent predictors of EHM after TACE. Among the multiphase CT radiomics models, the venous-phase random forest (RF) model performed best (AUC = 0.899, 95% CI: 0.799–0.998), outperforming the logistic regression (LR) and support vector machine (SVM) models. The combined clinical-radiomics model achieved an AUC of 0.923 in the internal test set, outperforming the clinical model alone. In the multicenter external validation cohort, the combined model yielded an AUC of 0.878 (95% CI: 0.801–0.957), indicating good generalizability. Conclusion The clinical-radiomics combined model, constructed from selected CT radiomic features and clinical features, demonstrated robust performance in predicting EHM in both the single-center development cohort and the multicenter external validation cohort. It holds promise for estimating the probability of EHM in patients with HCC after TACE and provides a noninvasive tool for preoperative risk stratification.

title: PRISM-Net: Patient-specific reference-guided inter-breast symmetry matching for three-class breast DCE-MRI classification
abstract: Abstract Breast DCE-MRI classification of breast sides as no lesion, benign, or malignant is complicated by substantial patient-specific variation in breast anatomy, tissue composition, and physiological enhancement. Although radiologists routinely use the contralateral breast as an internal reference, computational bilateral comparison remains challenging because corresponding contralateral regions are not anatomically identical and bilateral differences are not necessarily pathological. We propose PRISM-Net, a registration-free bilateral framework that treats the contralateral breast as an approximate patient-specific reference. PRISM-Net learns complementary target-appearance and reference-conditioned deviation representations. Adaptive patch-level matching constructs content-dependent contralateral references in a shared feature space without voxel-wise registration, while local-contrast reweighting emphasizes focal deviations over diffuse bilateral mismatch. The resulting deviation features are integrated with intrinsic target-side appearance through residual cross-attention and aggregated across slices for breast-side classification. On ODELIA, PRISM-Net achieved Macro AUC, Micro AUC, and quadratic weighted kappa values of 84.11 ± 2.33, 90.64 ± 1.61, and 60.94 ± 5.64 on the in-distribution test set, and 68.51 ± 4.54, 80.74 ± 2.68, and 43.45 ± 7.10 on the held-out institution, respectively, yielding the highest point estimates among the evaluated methods across the primary metrics. PRISM-Net also demonstrated favorable performance on an independent institutional cohort and background-complexity subsets, while ablation experiments supported the contributions of adaptive reference matching and focal deviation modeling. These findings support patient-specific contralateral reference learning as a clinically grounded strategy for breast DCE-MRI classification under heterogeneous background conditions.

title: Regional Trabecular Bone Alterations in Knee Osteoarthritis: QCT Evidence from the Knee and Lumbar Spine
abstract: Abstract Background Whether knee osteoarthritis (KOA)-related trabecular bone alterations are confined to the affected knee or also occur in the lumbar spine remains unclear. We compared regional knee and lumbar volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) between KOA patients and non-KOA controls, examined lower-limb alignment relationships with medial–lateral tibial vBMD distribution, and compared bone metabolism markers between groups. Methods This single-centre cross-sectional study included 46 participants (32 KOA, 14 controls). Quantitative computed tomography (QCT) measured trabecular vBMD at the medial and lateral tibial plateaus (TM, TL), medial and lateral femoral condyles (FM, FL), and lumbar spine (LS); the hip–knee–ankle angle (HKA) was measured on weight-bearing full-length radiographs. vBMD–KOA associations were examined with Firth penalised-likelihood logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index (BMI). Medial–lateral vBMD differences were assessed with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and between-group tibial vBMD distribution with a linear mixed-effects model. HKA–vBMD-difference associations used correlation and regression. title: Cross‑modal image‑text collaborative deep‑learning model for predicting severe coronary stenosis from CCTA: a retrospective single‑center study
abstract: Abstract Background Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a cornerstone non‑invasive modality for coronary artery evaluation. Nevertheless, conventional manual reading suffers from subjective bias and limited reproducibility. We proposed a cross‑modal deep‑learning framework integrating image and clinical text information to improve detection of severe coronary stenosis. Objective To develop and validate a cross‑modal radiomics deep‑learning model based on CCTA data and further evaluate its clinical performance for identifying severe coronary artery stenosis. Methods In this single‑center retrospective study, 96 patients receiving both CCTA and invasive coronary angiography (ICA) were enrolled, yielding 288 raw coronary vessel‑level samples; two vessels were excluded for vessel‑specific poor image quality, resulting in 286 evaluable coronary vessel‑level (unit of analysis) samples. A dual‑branch cross‑modal model combining ResNet‑18 image encoder and lightweight Transformer text encoder was constructed. Class‑differentiated augmentation and multi‑loss joint optimization were applied to mitigate class imbalance. Dataset was split into training/test set (8:2). Using ICA as reference gold‑standard, ROC‑based diagnostic metrics (AUC, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, PPV, NPV) were calculated for model and manual interpretation. Results Our cross‑modal deep‑learning model achieved AUC = 0.83 (95%CI 0.71‑0.94), sensitivity 64.0%, specificity 93.0%, accuracy 79.0%, PPV 89.0%, NPV 74.0%. It outperformed manual CCTA reading (AUC = 0.676; sensitivity 46.38%, specificity 88.7%, accuracy 68.5%). Conclusion The proposed cross‑modal image‑text collaborative deep‑learning model improves diagnostic performance for severe coronary stenosis. It could serve as a promising intelligent auxiliary tool for CCTA‑based non‑invasive assessment of coronary artery disease.

title: Quantifying Prematurity-Related Lung Disease in Adulthood using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) in adolescent sheep born premature: A pilot study
abstract: Abstract Background Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is known to offer the best structural and functional pulmonary assessment and is a promising tool for monitoring and tracking disease progression in prematurity-related lung disease (PRLD). Objective We aimed to test the feasibility of capturing anatomical correlates of PRLD with MRI using the bronchopulMonary rottErdam mRi morpholoGy scorE (MERGE-BPD score), and correlating imaging with histological, and functional, lung analysis. Materials and methods In this pilot study, 8 sheep from a larger cohort underwent pulmonary MRI at 1 year of age: 4 term-born lambs and 4 preterm-born lambs, of which two were exposed to intra-amniotic lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Besides MRI, lung function was measured using respiratory oscillometry, and histological analysis was performed on post-mortem lung tissue. Statistics were performed using the Kruskal-Wallis test and the Mann-Whitney test, and Z-scores were calculated. Results Areas of hyperintensity of lung parenchyma could be identified in all preterm-born animals and in one of the four term-born sheep. MRI changes are associated with histological changes driven by inflammation (− 0.97, 1.24, and 0.48 (overall p 0.04)) and mucus plugging (− 0.87, 0.86, and 0.82 (overall p 0.07)). Bronchial hyperreactivity was significantly different between the three groups (p 0.05). Conclusion We demonstrate that pulmonary MRI complements conventional lung function and histological analysis by detecting subtle abnormalities in prematurity-related lung diseases. It has the potential to become a valuable, safe, and radiation-free tool for predicting lung function trajectories in children and gaining a deeper understanding of pathophysiological mechanisms following preterm birth.

title: Automated Intracranial Aneurysm Detection and Size Extraction from Imaging Reports Using a Dual-Model Transformer Framework
abstract: Abstract Background The unstructured and variable nature of radiology reports remains a barrier to automated extraction of clinically relevant information for large-scale research and AI applications, particularly for intracranial aneurysms (IAs). Objective We aimed to develop and evaluate a dual-model transformer framework for intracranial aneurysm information extraction and assess whether structured processing improved classification and size-extraction performance compared with unstructured text. Methods We analyzed 3,183 neuroimaging reports annotated by neuroradiologists and neurosurgeons. Four encoder-based transformer models were evaluated for aneurysm-presence classification using 5-fold stratified cross-validation. A zero-shot Llama 3.1 framework was used to extract aneurysm size using direct and structured-report prompting. RadDistilBERT and Llama 3.1 were evaluated on 20 temporally distinct reports using full-report and impression-only inputs, with and without structured preprocessing. Results RadDistilBERT achieved the highest mean classification performance, with accuracy of 96.4% (± 1.8%), F1 score of 91.7% (± 10.3%), precision of 94.0% (± 4.6%), and recall of 90.7% (± 15.6%). F1 scores were 87.5% for BERT-base-uncased and 31.1% for ALBERT-base-v2. In the 20-report set, aneurysm-presence classification accuracy was 100% across all input and processing conditions. For aneurysm size extraction, structured report processing increased accuracy from 61.90% to 66.67% using the full report and from 80.95% to 85.00% using the impression section. Conclusions This study demonstrates the feasibility of a dual-model transformer framework for aneurysm-presence classification and size extraction from unstructured neuroimaging reports. RadDistilBERT achieved the strongest classification performance, while Llama 3.1 enabled zero-shot size extraction. These findings support further external validation and expansion to additional aneurysm characteristics with dedicated annotation and validation.

title: Distance-to-Ventricle Guided Deep Learning for Periventricular and Deep Multiple Sclerosis Lesion Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Periventricular lesions are central to the diagnosis of multiple sclerosis (MS), but automatic segmentation is the least dependable. Whether a lesion is periventricular (PV) or deep is said by its three-dimensional distance to the ventricles. We show that on a thick-slice clinical MRI this decision depends on the ventricles in adjacent slices and on the slice spacing, so that an in-plane distance would show 30% of PV lesion voxels as deep. We therefore give the geometry explicitly. A 3D distance-to-ventricle map, computed in millimetres on the full volume, is added in as one of the input channel to a 2.5D U-Net that segments ventricles, normal white matter hyperintensities (WMH), PV lesions and deep lesions. On the 100-patient MS3SEG dataset, against an identically trained baseline, the distance model raised held-out Dice for PV lesions from 0.731 to 0.758 and for deep lesions from 0.702 to 0.738 (Holm-corrected p < 0.001) and reduced PV/deep label confusions by 71%, while the pooled lesion Dice was unchanged. Ablation and counterfactual analyses shows that the prior improves the structural assignment of lesions rather than their detection itself.

title: Molecular Findings, Clinical Severity, and Transplant-Free Survival in Pediatric Cardiomyopathy: A Prospective Indian Cohort
abstract: Abstract Background The relationship between molecular findings, clinical disease severity, and heart failure (HF) outcomes in pediatric cardiomyopathy remains uncertain. Objectives To evaluate genetic diagnostic yield and the relative associations of clinical severity, biomarkers, and multimodality imaging with death or heart transplantation in children with cardiomyopathy. Methods This prospective single-center study included 235 children younger than 18 years at a South Indian referral center. Genetic testing, HF functional class, biomarkers, echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), and longitudinal outcomes were evaluated. Transplant-free survival was assessed using Kaplan–Meier analysis and Cox regression. Hierarchical models evaluated incremental prognostic discrimination using Harrell's C-index. Results Genetic testing was performed in 112 children (47.7%), of whom 54 (48.2%) had reported pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants. During a median follow-up of 15 months, 63 children (26.8%) died or underwent heart transplantation. Transplant-free survival did not differ significantly between P/LP-positive and genetic-negative groups (log-rank P = 0.058). Reduced ventricular function and late gadolinium enhancement were associated with adverse outcomes in univariable analyses. Among complete cases, the apparent C-index increased from 0.527 for demographics and cardiomyopathy phenotype to 0.813 after adding HF functional class and 0.842 after biomarkers, with limited additional discrimination from imaging measures. Conclusions Genetic testing demonstrated substantial laboratory-reported P/LP yield, although its effects on clinical management, family screening, and costs were not evaluated. HF functional severity and biomarkers provided the greatest apparent prognostic discrimination for death or transplantation, supporting an integrated clinical approach to pediatric cardiomyopathy assessment.

title: Performance and Reliability Assessment of Deep Learning Models for OCT-Based Retinal Disease Classification
abstract: Abstract Background Deep learning models have achieved high classification accuracy on OCT images for discriminating among retinal diseases. However, clinical OCT datasets often exhibit substantial class imbalance, and aggregate metrics may obscure unreliable predictions for underrepresented classes. The reliability of such models for clinical decision support therefore remains uncertain. This study aimed to comprehensively assess the reliability of a deep learning-based OCT model under class imbalance. Methods Ten public OCT datasets were combined for a nine-class classification task of normal retina and eight retinal diseases. A Swin Transformer model was developed and evaluated on an internal test set, two independent public test sets (DUKE and OCTID), and a prospective clinical OCT cohort. Class-specific performance and bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals were analyzed alongside conventional metrics. Expected calibration error (ECE) assessed the reliability of predicted probabilities. LayerCAM was used to examine model attention to disease-related structures, and UMAP to visualized the deep feature space. Results On the internal test set, the model achieved a macro-AUC of 0.9992 and macro-recall of 0.9886. Despite high recall for some underrepresented classes, bootstrap estimates of precision and F1-score varied more widely, underscoring the need to consider sample size and uncertainty. Macro-F1 scores were 0.9884 on DUKE and 0.8944 on OCTID; recall for the underrepresented CSC class on OCTID was 0.7863. Pre-calibration ECE was 0.0048, indicating good agreement between predicted probabilities and observed outcomes. In the clinical cohort, macro-F1 was 0.8813 and macro-recall was 0.8365. LayerCAM activations corresponded spatially to disease-related retinal structures in many cases. UMAP showed class-specific clustering, with some overlap between classes. Conclusion This study assessed the reliability of deep learning-based OCT models for retinal disease discrimination under class imbalance. Overall performance alone is insufficient to characterize model reliability in multi-disease clinical settings. Class-specific stability, uncertainty, probability calibration, and interpretability also warrant assessment. These findings support a risk-aware decision-support strategy in which model outputs are interpreted together with class representation and uncertainty, and uncertain or underrepresented cases are flagged for specialist review. Prospective human–AI studies are needed before clinical deployment.

title: Case report: First report of hydrocephalus in free-living grey wolf (Canis lupus) pup
abstract: Abstract Background: Hydrocephalus is a neurological disorder characterized by abnormal accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) within the brain ventricles. It may be congenital or result from infections or trauma. This condition is relatively well documented in dogs; however, little is known about its occurrence in wild animals. Nevertheless, the justification for treating affected wild individuals is often debatable, which highlights the importance of rapid, accurate diagnosis. Case presentation: A grey wolf (Canis lupus) pup, approximately two months old, was found near a village in southern Poland. Due to unsuccessful reintroduction attempts, the animal was admitted to a wildlife rehabilitation center. Neurological signs prompted a detailed clinical examination, and computed tomography (CT) of the head confirmed hydrocephalus. Given the severity of neurological deficits, their presumed congenital origin, and the lack of treatment options compatible with survival in the wild, the prognosis was poor. Euthanasia was therefore considered the most appropriate option based on animal welfare considerations. Reintroduction was deemed impossible, and prolonged captivity did not meet acceptable welfare standards for this species. Conclusion: This case highlights the importance of rapid diagnosis in wild animals and contributes to the limited data on hydrocephalus in free-ranging species, supporting decision-making in wildlife rehabilitation centers and improving understanding of mortality factors in wild populations.

title: Chest Computed Tomography Habitat and Body Composition for Survival Prediction in Stage IV Lung Cancer
abstract: Abstract Objectives To integrate clinical characteristics, CT habitat radiomic features, and quantitative body composition parameters in patients with stage IV non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and develop a multidimensional model for predicting overall survival. Materials and methods Overall, 196 patients with stage IV NSCLC were retrospectively enrolled and divided into a training set (n = 137) and an internal test set (n = 59). An additional 50 patients formed an external test set. Radiomic features of the entire tumor, tumor habitat features based on K-means clustering, and body composition at the L3 vertebral level were extracted using 3D Slicer. Random forest and LASSO(LASSO) regression were utilized for feature selection, followed by the construction of unimodal, bimodal, and multi-dimensional integrated prognostic models. Model performance was evaluated via Harrell’s concordance index, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and Kaplan–Meier survival analysis. The SHapley Additive exPlanations(SHAP) method was used for model interpretability analysis. Results The multidimensional fusion model achieved the best performance, with area under the curve values of 0.842, 0.811, and 0.817 in the training, internal, and external test sets, respectively. It significantly outperformed single-modality models and effectively stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups (log-rank p = 0.00067). C-indices were 0.850, 0.790, and 0.760, respectively. SHAP analysis identified body composition features as key contributors to survival prediction. Conclusion The proposed model demonstrated robust prognostic performance and may support individualized management of advanced NSCLC.

title: Zero-shot performance of a concept-grounded chest radiograph foundation model depends on the evaluation dataset: a preregistered external evaluation of CLEAR and CheXzero
abstract: Abstract CLEAR, a concept-grounded vision-language model presented as auditable, scores chest radiographs through 368,294 radiological concepts. It reportedly outperformed CheXzero in zero-shot classification, but only on developer-chosen test sets, without a subgroup analysis or a systematic check of the concepts behind its zero-shot predictions. In a preregistered comparison on the NIH ChestX-ray14 test split (25,592 images, 2,797 patients), macro-AUROC over 14 findings was 0.695 for CheXzero, 0.635 for CLEAR's concept route and 0.700 for direct scoring with CLEAR's encoder. Neither model showed evidence of a sex gap (female minus male: CheXzero + 0.005, 95% CI − 0.015 to + 0.022; concept route − 0.008, − 0.029 to + 0.011) or an age gap under any of four prompt templates. Prompt wording alone reversed the ranking of CLEAR's direct route against CheXzero (− 0.038 to + 0.031). The concept space was nearly collapsed (participation ratio 2.95, against 11.18 for the image features), and one held-out-selected concept outperformed the concept route for every finding. On the Indiana University collection, one of CLEAR's own test sets, it trailed CheXzero by 0.015 (0.007 to 0.024), using report indexing terms as labels. CLEAR's zero-shot advantage depended on the dataset, and the concept step added no accuracy over the image encoder. Developer-reported zero-shot gains and concept explanations need independent testing before health systems adopt them.

title: Integrating Deep Learning Radiomics and Node-RADS for Interpretable Prediction of Colorectal Cancer Lymph Node Metastasis
abstract: Abstract Background and purpose: To develop and validate an interpretable multimodal fusion model integrating deep learning radiomics (DLR) and Node-RADS score for preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in colorectal cancer (CRC). Methods: This retrospective multicenter study included 892 CRC patients (training: Center 1, n=684; external validation: Centers 2/3, n=208). Venous-phase CT tumor regions were segmented. 1394 radiomic and 320 ResNet-50 deep learning features were extracted; LASSO was used for feature selection. An XGBoost DLR model was integrated with Node-RADS score and clinical variables to construct a multimodal nomogram. Performance was assessed by AUC, calibration, decision curve analysis, and the DeLong test. SHAP analysis provided model interpretability. Results: LASSO regression identified 24 deep learning features and 9 radiomic features with non-zero coefficients, wherein deep learning features demonstrated higher predictive weights. The XGBoost-based DLR model achieved AUCs of 0.876 and 0.798 in training and external validation cohorts, respectively. The multimodal fusion model, incorporating Node-RADS score and selected imaging features, yielded significantly improved AUCs of 0.900 (95%CI:0.874–0.926) and 0.870 (95%CI:0.821–0.919), outperforming both the DLR model and the clinical model (AUC 0.751/0.641) (all DeLong P< 0.05). Calibration curves demonstrated excellent agreement (Hosmer–Lemeshow P > 0.05), and decision curve analysis confirmed superior net clinical benefit across wide threshold ranges. SHAP analysis identified DL_27 and lbp_3D_m2_glszm_ZoneEntropy as the dominant predictive features. Conclusion: This externally validated, interpretable CT-based multimodal model integrating DLR signatures and Node-RADS score enables accurate preoperative prediction of LNM in CRC, offering a noninvasive decision-support tool to guide personalized treatment.

title: Explainable, Uncertainty-Aware Ensemble Learning for Brain Tumor Classification from MRI with a Simulated Fairness Audit
abstract: Abstract Most brain MRI classifiers stop at accuracy; whether their explanations hold up, how sure each call is and whether some patients fare worse is rarely checked. We combined five convolutional networks (Xception, InceptionV3, EfficientNetB4, DenseNet121 and ConvNeXtTiny) and a ViT-B/16 transformer through a logistic regression meta-learner fitted on Out-of-Fold predictions. The models were trained with five-fold cross-validation on 5,040 of 7,200 class-balanced MRI images and tested once on 1,080 held-out images. The MetaEnsemble reached 98.33% accuracy, an AUC-ROC of 0.9989 and an Expected Calibration Error of 0.0083, whereas every single model was underconfident. We set LIME, SHAP, Grad-CAM and Grad-CAM + + side by side and scored the Grad-CAM maps (localization accuracy, Pointing Game accuracy, AOPC faithfulness) instead of judging them by eye. Forty Monte Carlo Dropout passes per image gave each case an uncertainty estimate. Lacking patient metadata, we simulated age and sex labels from epidemiological priors to demonstrate a fairness audit; the gaps were small but pointed the same way in every model (age 1.55% to 4.00%, sex 1.07% to 2.05%). The evidence comes from one public dataset, but it shows that explanation scoring, uncertainty estimation and subgroup checks can be planned into a brain tumor classifier from the start.

title: Single-Projection Three-Dimensional X-ray Imaging through Time- and Energy-Resolved Photon Scattering
abstract: Abstract Scattered X-ray photons contain information about material composition but are generally treated as contamination in conventional computed tomography (CT). We investigate a theoretical time- and energy-encoded CT framework that uses photon arrival time, position, and energy to localize scattering events and reconstruct three-dimensional Rayleigh and Compton scattering distributions from a single projection without mechanical rotation. The framework was evaluated using Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations of heterogeneous tissue, head-and-neck, and high-resolution pattern phantoms. Under idealized source and detector conditions, the reconstructed scattering distributions differentiated soft tissues and reproduced simulated structures, including features as small as 0.1 mm. Quantitative errors of approximately 1–7% and a simulated dose of 50 µGy were reported for the investigated configurations. These results establish the information-reconstruction potential of time- and energy-resolved scatter measurements, rather than the performance of a realizable clinical scanner. Implementation will require ultrashort X-ray pulses, precise photon timing and energy measurements, and adequate detector coverage. The approach provides a theoretical basis for investigating single-projection volumetric X-ray scatter imaging and material characterization.

title: Prediction of Lymphovascular Invasion in Breast Cancer Using Intratumoral and Peritumoral MRI Radiomics Models Based on DCE-MRI: A Multicenter Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose This study explores the predictive value of intramural and peritumoral radiomics features based on dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) for lymphovascular invasion (LVI) in breast cancer. It compares the predictive efficacy of different peritumoral regions and feature fusion methods, and constructs a combined prediction model integrating clinical characteristics. Materials and Methods Retrospectively collected images from 757 breast cancer patients with pathologically confirmed diagnoses who underwent breast DCE-MRI examinations at two medical centers. Data from Center 1 served as the training set (n = 529), while data from Center 2 formed the external validation set (n = 228). Tumor lesions were semi-automatically delineated using ITK-SNAP software, with peritumoral regions automatically expanded. Regions of interest (ROIs) were selected on the maximum intensity phase of DCE-MRI. Radiomics features were extracted using PyRadiomics across four modalities: intratumoral, peritumoral (1mm, 3mm, 5mm, 7mm, 10mm, 15mm, 20mm), Tumor+Peri7mm, and ImageFusion7 (a fusion of tumor and optimal 7mm peritumoral regions). Data dimensionality reduction and feature selection were performed using Spearman correlation analysis, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression, and Maximum Relevance-Minimum Redundancy (mRMR) methods. Five classifiers—support vector machine (SVM), extreme trees (ET), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and multilayer perceptron (MLP)—were evaluated under different feature models to identify the optimal classifier for constructing the radiomics model. Clinical Features: Single- and multi-factor logistic regression screened clinical risk factors to construct a clinical model. Comprehensive evaluations were conducted on the clinical model, the optimal radiomic model, and a combined model incorporating clinical features with optimal radiomic features. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves analyzed predictive performance, with area under the curve (AUC) calculated. A fusion model was established by integrating the radiomic score (rad-score) from the highest-performing predictive model and visualized via a nomogram. The clinical utility of the predictive models was assessed using calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Clinical characteristics: The AUC values of the clinical model based on histological grade, sentinel lymph node status, and TIC were 0.738 (95% CI: 0.6949–0.7802) and 0.749 (95% CI: 0.6830–0.8141) in the training and validation sets, respectively. As a key indicator reflecting lymph node metastasis in primary tumors, sentinel lymph node status is widely recognized for its role in breast cancer staging and prognostic assessment. For instance, in breast cancer, the area under the ROC curve for a non-sentinel lymph node metastasis risk prediction model in sentinel lymph node-positive patients reached 0.7613, demonstrating its clinical utility. Radiomics: Among the various peritumoral models, the 7 mm peritumoral model demonstrated the best performance. Results indicate that the radiomics model based on the ImageFusion7 (intra-tumor and peritumoral image fusion region) demonstrated optimal diagnostic performance, with the XGBoost classifier showing particularly outstanding results: an AUC of 0.861 (95% CI: 0.8302–0.8914) in the training set and an AUC of 0.709 (95% CI: 0.6407–0.7768). When constructing a clinical-imaging fusion model, the ROC curve based on clinical features and Radscore values achieved AUC values of 0.892 (95% CI: 0.8629–0.9165) and 0.778 (95% CI: 0.7140–0.8375) in the training and validation sets, respectively, surpassing all single models and the intra-tumoral/peritumoral model. The DCA curve demonstrated that the combined model exhibited the highest clinical efficacy and closely followed the diagonal line in the calibration curve, indicating superior model fit and generalization capability. Conclusions An image-based model utilizing DCE-MRI effectively predicts lymphovascular invasion (LVI) status in breast cancer, with the ImageFusion7 model—which integrates images from both the tumor interior and a 7mm peritumoral region—demonstrating optimal predictive performance. Combining this model with clinically independent risk factors further enhances its accuracy. The constructed fusion model exhibits strong discriminatory power and clinical applicability, providing a valuable tool for non-invasive preoperative assessment of LVI risk.

title: Prediction of ERCC1 Expression Level in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Based on Multi-sequence MRI Radiomics and Habitat Analysis
abstract: Abstract Objective To explore the value of multi-sequence MRI-derived radiomics and habitat analysis for predicting excision repair cross-complementation group 1 (ERCC1) expression in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Methods In this retrospective study, 171 patients with non-keratinizing undifferentiated NPC without distant metastasis were enrolled. Patients were stratified into high-ERCC1 (n = 75) and low-ERCC1 (n = 96) groups and randomly split into training (n = 136) and test (n = 35) sets at an 8:2 ratio. Radiomic and habitat features were extracted from T1WI, CE-T1WI and T2WI to calculate radscore and habitat radscore. We constructed radiomics, habitat, clinical, radiomics-clinical and habitat-clinical combined models. Results A total of 14 radiomic features and 20 habitat features were finally selected. Clinical stage (OR = 1.828, 95%CI: 1.011–3.305, P = 0.046) was identified as an independent predictor of high ERCC1 expression. Based on this predictor, five models were constructed: radiomics model, habitat model, radiomics-clinical model, habitat-clinical model and clinical model. Their area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values in the training set were 0.825, 0.917, 0.830, 0.922 and 0.605, respectively; the corresponding AUC values in the test set were 0.770, 0.787, 0.770, 0.807 and 0.537. All radiomics-based models yielded higher AUC values than the clinical model (De Long test, all P < 0.05). The habitat model outperformed the conventional radiomics model in the training set (De Long test, P < 0.05)). Conclusions The Multi-sequence MRI-based radiomics and habitat analysis enable effective prediction of ERCC1 expression in NPC patients. The habitat-clinical model achieved the best predictive performance and may support clinical decision-making and prognostic evaluation. The habitat model was superior to conventional radiomics models, suggesting that refined sub-regional segmentation can help boost radiomics prediction accuracy.

title: Pulmonary artery intimal sarcoma misdiagnosed as pulmonary embolism: MDM2 amplification as the diagnostic anchor in an unresectable tumor—a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Pulmonary artery intimal sarcoma (PAIS) is a rare and aggressive vascular malignancy whose clinical and radiological features overlap with those of pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE); most patients are initially anticoagulated, and no standard systemic therapy exists for unresectable disease. Amplification of MDM2 is the defining genomic event, yet it is usually treated as a supplementary finding rather than as a diagnostic test. Case presentation A 51-year-old man without thromboembolic risk factors presented with cough, sputum production, and chest discomfort. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) showed filling defects extending from the main pulmonary artery into both branches together with a 5.0 × 2.7 cm left upper lobe mass, and he received rivaroxaban until hemoptysis occurred. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET)/CT showed concordant hypermetabolism of the intravascular and parenchymal lesions. Two biopsies, including an expert review, narrowed the differential only to intimal sarcoma versus sarcomatoid carcinoma; next-generation sequencing then identified MDM2 amplification with CDKN2A deletion, a low tumor mutational burden (1.95 mutations/Mb), and negative PD-L1 expression, establishing MDM2-driven PAIS. Because the tumor was unresectable, he received six cycles of sintilimab, docetaxel, and cisplatin, two further cycles of sintilimab and docetaxel, consolidative intensity-modulated radiotherapy (60 Gy in 25 fractions), and maintenance sintilimab monotherapy. The best response was stable disease with a 27.9% reduction in the sum of target-lesion diameters, and progression-free survival reached 12.1 months without grade ≥3 immune-related adverse events. Conclusions When morphology and immunohistochemistry are indeterminate, MDM2 amplification can be the decisive diagnostic test rather than a supplementary finding, and it should be sought before empirical treatment is committed. Chemotherapy-primed PD-1 blockade followed by consolidative radiotherapy produced durable disease control in an immunologically cold tumor; prospective registries are needed to test this sequence.

title: Splenic Abscess Masquerading as Left Lobar Pneumonia: Early Detection with Point-of- Care Ultrasound in the Emergency Department – a case report
abstract: Abstract Splenic abscess is a rare but potentially life-threatening intra-abdominal infection that often presents with nonspecific symptoms, leading to frequent misdiagnosis and delayed treatment. Thoracoabdominal pain, particularly on the left side, may mimic respiratory conditions such as pneumonia. We report a case of a 22-year-old male who presented with one week of left-sided chest and upper abdominal pain, low-grade fever, and anorexia. He was initially treated as having left lobar pneumonia. However, bedside point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) performed in the emergency department revealed a wedge-shaped hypoechoic lesion in the spleen, prompting further investigation. Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT confirmed a large subcapsular splenic abscess with mass effect on adjacent organs. Laboratory studies showed marked leukocytosis (WBC 28 ×10³/µL) with left shift and elevated ESR (120 mm/hr). Transthoracic echocardiography showed no vegetations. The patient was managed with abscess drainage, broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, later tailored to culture and sensitivity. The patient was symptom-free during follow-up with normal investigations and no residual collection. At follow-up, the patient was clinically well, repeat laboratory investigations were unremarkable, and ultrasound showed no residual splenic collection. This case underscores the diagnostic challenge of splenic abscess and highlights the critical role of POCUS in early emergency diagnosis

title: Benefits of thyroid screening and evidence suggesting radiation exposure as a cause of increased pediatric thyroid cancer in Fukushima Prefecture
abstract: Abstract The Fukushima Daiichi nuclear accident released a large quantity of radioactive materials, including radioactive iodine, which can cause thyroid cancer. Following the accident, Fukushima Prefecture conducted thyroid ultrasound examinations (TUEs) among approximately 380,000 individuals aged 18 years or younger or in utero at the time of the accident. The thyroid cancer (TC) incidence detected through this program was several dozen times higher than the national average, raising concerns regarding screening effects, overdiagnosis, and whether to reduce or discontinue the program. However, the clinical benefits of TUEs remain unclear. Using data from the NPO 311Fund, which supports patients inside and outside Fukushima, we evaluated the clinical implications of screening. Compared with patients diagnosed clinically after symptomatic presentation, those identified through screening exhibited approximately one-fifth the total thyroidectomy rate, one-sixth the rate of distant metastasis, and 40% of the radioiodine therapy rate. Furthermore, a strong positive correlation was observed between regional radiation dose estimates and TC incidence (R² = 0.9723, p = 0.014). title: Preoperative Bone Marrow Lesion Severity and Early Quality of Recovery After Medial Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background The prognostic significance of preoperative bone marrow lesions (BMLs) after medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) remains uncertain. This study investigated the association between preoperative medial BML severity and early postoperative quality of recovery. Methods This single-centre retrospective cohort study included 173 patients who underwent medial UKA between December 2024 and August 2025. Preoperative magnetic resonance imaging was used to calculate a composite medial BML score ranging from 0 to 6. Patients were classified into no-BML (n = 36), mild (n = 60), moderate (n = 42), and severe (n = 35) groups. The primary outcome was the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score at discharge. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain area under the curve (AUC), knee circumference change, and Knee Society Scores (KSS) at 3, 6, and 12 months. Associations were assessed using Spearman correlation and multivariable linear regression with HC3 robust standard errors. False discovery rate (FDR) adjustment across 20 outcomes was performed as a sensitivity analysis. Results Mean discharge QoR-15 scores were 134.92 ± 6.87, 132.98 ± 6.70, 130.62 ± 8.76, and 130.17 ± 9.14 across increasing BML severity groups (P = 0.031). After covariate adjustment, each one-point increase in BML score was associated with a 0.755-point decrease in QoR-15 (95% CI − 1.384 to − 0.125; P = 0.019) and a 0.125-cm increase in postoperative knee circumference change (95% CI 0.010–0.241; P = 0.034). Neither association remained statistically significant after FDR adjustment (q = 0.125 and q = 0.169, respectively). No clear associations were observed with postoperative pain AUC or KSS during the first postoperative year. Conclusions Greater preoperative medial BML severity showed nominal associations with poorer early recovery quality and greater postoperative knee swelling, although these findings did not remain statistically significant after multiplicity adjustment. By examining discharge QoR-15 rather than solely knee-specific outcomes, this study addresses a less-explored dimension of recovery after medial UKA. Further prospective validation is required before medial BML severity can be used as an independent prognostic indicator.

title: Parameter-Efficient Mask-Conditioned Magnetic Resonance Image Synthesis for Segmentation Augmentation
abstract: Abstract When real training images for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) segmentation are limited, existing masks can be reused to synthesize additional image appearances. However, paired image-translation methods may favor pixel fidelity over distributional similarity, while full diffusion-model fine-tuning is costly and generic conditioning does not explicitly encode mask geometry. To address these limitations, we propose ControlNet-guided Low-Rank Adaptation for MRI synthesis (\method), a mask-conditioned latent diffusion framework that adapts both the denoising and spatial-conditioning pathways. Only 2.96\% of the framework parameters are trainable in the BraTS configuration. We evaluate image quality and segmentation utility on BraTS2020 brain MRI and ACDC cardiac MRI across four fractions of real training slices. On BraTS T1 contrast-enhanced MRI, \method achieves a lower FID than Pix2Pix (55.65 versus 162.42), although Pix2Pix has higher paired pixel fidelity. With 10\% real training slices, adding synthetic pairs raises mean Dice from 0.7208 to 0.7401 and reduces HD95 from 48.43 to 45.34 pixels in a within-cohort, slice-level BraTS evaluation. On 50 held-out ACDC patients, a separately trained adapter raises mean Dice from 0.7661 to 0.8263 and reduces HD95 from 15.40 to 13.63 pixels at the same fraction. Gains diminish as real-image availability increases. These results support targeted use of parameter-efficient, mask-conditioned MRI synthesis when real-image coverage is low.

title: Interpretable multimodal deep learning for diagnosis and symptom-onset prediction in genetic frontotemporal dementia
abstract: Abstract Background: Genetic frontotemporal dementia (FTD) is characterized by substantial clinical and neuroanatomical heterogeneity, making prediction of symptom onset challenging. We evaluated whether deep learning-derived MRI biomarkers could be combined with non-imaging biomarkers in an interpretable framework for diagnosis and phenoconversion prediction in genetic FTD. Methods: We evaluated Multi-ICNN, a multimodal extension of the Interpretable Convolutional Neural Network, using data from the FTD Risk Cohort. Imaging biomarkers derived from T1-weighted MRI were combined with demographic, genetic, and neuropsychological biomarkers in an additive prediction model. We evaluated classification of symptomatic mutation carriers versus genetically confirmed non-carriers and phenoconversion prediction within 2- and 5-year time horizons. Biomarker contributions were examined at the group and participant levels. Results: For diagnosis, Multi-ICNN achieved the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.953, numerically outperforming the single-modality models. For phenoconversion prediction, the deep learning-based models outperformed the conventional volumetric and non-imaging models. The imaging-only ICNN achieved the highest mean AUCs of 0.798 and 0.780 for the 2- and 5-year horizons, respectively. Adding non-imaging biomarkers did not further improve ICNN performance. Neuropsychological measures contributed most strongly to diagnosis, whereas imaging-derived biomarkers dominated phenoconversion prediction, particularly biomarkers involving frontal and temporal regions. The additive model also provided participant-specific biomarker contributions. Conclusions: Interpretable deep learning-derived MRI biomarkers showed promise for phenoconversion prediction in genetic FTD, while the value of multimodal integration depended on the clinical task. The main limitations were the modest sample size and lack of external validation, reflecting the rarity of genetic FTD and the limited availability of comparable longitudinal cohorts.

title: Deep Generative Models Meet Federated Learning: A Healthcare-Centered Review
abstract: Abstract The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare holds significant promise, yet remains constrained by data scarcity, privacy and ethical concerns, and the inherent complexity of medical tasks. This review explores the intersection of deep generative modeling and federated learning, two complementary paradigms that enable collaborative and privacy-preserving innovation. We survey a total of 85 articles on recent trends in deep generative models for healthcare, with a special focus on federated settings. The review is structured around model architectures, providing a taxonomy-driven analysis that emphasizes solutions tailored to the heterogeneity of healthcare data. The current literature is largely limited to single-modality models; multimodal frameworks have only emerged over the last three years of our 7-year scope ($n=14$), where they are beginning to gain traction. Among deep generative approaches, generative adversarial networks dominate the field, particularly in medical image synthesis, where they comprise 66\% of the studies. While alternative architectures such as variational autoencoders remain marginally represented in federated healthcare scenarios, diffusion and autoregressive models are gaining importance, suggesting a paradigm shift in the near future. Notably, the number of related publications has increased substantially in recent years, rising from 1 in 2020 to as many as 31 in 2025, with 2026 pointing toward a similar trend, reflecting the growing interest and momentum in this area. This paper highlights key challenges, open research questions, and future directions for the development of robust, distributed generative AI in healthcare.

title: MEFV Genetic Variants and Acute Abdominal Presentations in Adults Undergoing Genetic Testing for Familial Mediterranean Fever: A Retrospective Single-Center Study
abstract: Abstract Background Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) is an inherited autoinflammatory disease characterized by recurrent attacks of fever and serosal inflammation. The relationship between MEFV genetic characteristics and acute abdominal outcomes remains incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the associations between MEFV variants and emergency department presentations, abdominal computed tomography (CT) abnormalities, and surgical intervention in adults with detected MEFV variants. Methods This retrospective single-center study included 171 adults with at least one detected MEFV variant who underwent MEFV testing between January 1, 2021 and December 31, 2024. Demographic characteristics, MEFV variant number and type, zygosity, ACMG classification, emergency department presentations for abdominal pain, abdominal CT findings, and surgical intervention were retrospectively assessed. Group comparisons used parametric, nonparametric, and exact tests as appropriate (p < 0.05). Results Among 171 patients, 66.7% were female; mean age was 37.99 ± 14.13 years. One MEFV variant was detected in 129 patients (75.4%), two variants in 41 (24.0%), and four variants in one patient (0.6%). M694V was the most frequent single variant. Sixty-five patients (38.0%) presented to the emergency department with abdominal pain during the study period. Fourteen patients (8.2%) had abdominal CT abnormalities. All patients with CT abnormalities presented to the emergency department, versus 32.5% of those without ( p = 0.001). Surgical intervention was performed in four patients (2.3%). Surgery was more frequent with CT abnormalities (14.3% vs 1.3%; p = 0.025). All four patients who underwent surgery had an emergency department presentation ( p = 0.005), and the number of emergency department visits was higher in the surgical group ( p = 0.028). Specific MEFV variants were not significantly associated with emergency department presentation or surgical intervention. Conclusions Specific MEFV variants and the number of detected variants were not significantly associated with emergency department utilization or surgical intervention in this cohort. In contrast, abdominal CT abnormalities were associated with emergency department presentations and were associated with a higher frequency of surgical intervention. Larger prospective studies are warranted.

title: High burden of treatment-requiring retinopathy of prematurity in Kathmandu, Nepal: a prospective multicentre observational study
abstract: Abstract Background: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is an important cause of avoidable childhood blindness in low- and middle-income countries, where increasing survival of preterm infants has outpaced improvements in neonatal care. We assessed the frequency, severity and treatment requirements of ROP across neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) and specialist eye centres in the Kathmandu Valley. Methods: This prospective multi-centre observational cohort study was conducted from February–November 2025 at two level III NICUs and two tertiary eye centres in Kathmandu. Preterm infants with a gestational age (GA) <34 weeks and/or a birth weight (BW) <2000 g, and infants of 34–36 weeks GA with risk factors, were enrolled. Bilateral wide-field retinal imaging was performed at serial examinations and ROP was classified according to ICROP-3. The primary outcome was development of type 1 ROP. Baseline characteristics were compared between infants who developed type 1 ROP and those with type 2 ROP or no ROP using t-tests and chi-square tests, with odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for factors estimated for prespecified factors associated with type 1 ROP. Results: Of 222 infants who underwent at least one ROP examination, 208 completed follow-up to complete retinal vascularisation or disease resolution. Among these 208 infants, 76 (36.5%) developed ROP, including 46 (22.1%) with type 1 ROP and 30 (14.4%) with type 2 ROP. Aggressive posterior ROP (A-ROP) occurred in 14 (6.7%) infants. Infants who developed type 1 ROP had lower mean GA and BW than those with type 2 ROP or no ROP. BW ≤1500 g was associated with type 1 ROP (OR 2.99, 95% CI 1.73–5.18). Type 1 ROP was more frequently observed among infants screened at specialist eye centres than NICUs (OR 3.12, 95% CI 1.67–5.80), although this comparison may reflect referral selection. ROP was present at the first examination in 60 of 222 infants (27.0%). 3/25 infants (12.0%) outside the principal enrollment thresholds developed ROP, including 1/25 (4.0%) with type 1 ROP. Conclusions: ROP, including Type 1 disease, was frequently observed, with some cases detected at the initial screening and among infants beyond conventional eligibility criteria, underscoring the need for Nepal-specific screening guidelines and strengthened referral pathways. Trial registration: Registered as https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN62477762on the date 02/11/2025
